# The gap ledger (authoritative, kept current in the same change as any acceptance or tripwire)

> **MEMORY SIZING (Ada 2026-11-20: the daemon held 7.1 GB resident after an 84 MB Mercurial push; w-sizing).** Every
> buffer, region, reserve and prefault is sized from the work, learned, decays and is given back; a machine total is
> only a ceiling. **A-765 BUILT:** an idle shard's prefault reserve (A-214) decays: the last burst whole for one sweep
> interval, then halved each interval (`daemon::decayed_reserve`); before, the burst was held whole for as long as the
> shard stayed idle (macOS arm64, Studio-4: a 64 MiB burst still reserved whole after 20 s idle; after, 0 and 234 MB
> given back). **Measure the footprint on macOS, not RSS:** a given-back page of a shared object leaves the footprint
> but stays in RSS and vmmap's resident until the kernel wants it (a 64 MiB `shm_open` probe: footprint 64 -> 0 MiB,
> RSS 64 -> 64); `slates_machine::facts::resident_now`, which the pressure hold's own growth reads, is RSS (open).
> **Open, by size:**
> `reserve_per_shard` = memory / shards / 3 sizes each shard's slice of the content object (write log R/4, image slots
> 2R, delta log R, arena R: about 1.4 times the machine's memory of address space, ~220 GB on the 96 GB Studio, g226),
> the reserve's ceiling, the DAX table, the client and fleet shares; the sweep of every sizing site follows here.
> **The sweep (w-sizing, 2026-11-20, by reading origin/main 6337049f6; today -> what it should be):**
> - The root: `reserve_per_shard` = min(memory.total, the OS/job/cgroup bound) / shards / 3 (`config.rs`
>   `DaemonConfig::derive`, `slates_mem::budget::region_bytes`). Machine-derived, fixed at boot. Every size below
>   derives from it. -> Split its two roles: an admission ceiling learned from the work and the device's pressure (the
>   machine total only a ceiling), and address space reserved by what is stored, not by the ceiling.
> - The content object's address space, per shard (`shard_content_layout`): write log R/4, two image slots 2R, delta
>   log R, DAX table, arena R; about 4.25R a shard, 1.4 times memory in all (220 GB mapped on the 96 GB Studio, g226;
>   16 GiB mapped on w-hg's run). -> Image slots and the delta log sized from the image a shard publishes (metadata),
>   grown by doubling; the arena grown by pool extents (A-98) as content arrives; the write log from the measured
>   write stream between barriers.
> - The idle prefault reserve (A-214): the last burst, capped at R. A-765 decays it; w-hg's release run held 4,931.4
>   MiB resident after hg's history push and faulted 3.5 GB more at idle. -> Removed unless the A/B (prefault vs none,
>   R9 provisioning p99, RSS) shows it pays; if it does, an EWMA of the pages a turn touches.
> - Tables from R: `table_bytes` (R x TABLE_SHARE), `max_inodes`, `max_dirs`, `max_chunks`, `metadata_class_bytes`,
>   the volume record bound. -> Grown on demand (doubling, given back on shrink), bounded by admission, not
>   preallocated from R.
> - Shares of R: `clients_per_shard` (R x CLIENT_SHARE / region), the NFSv4 client share and slots, the fleet receive
>   windows (R x FLEET_RECEIVE_SHARE), `dax_range_slots` (R / DAX_RANGE_BYTES), the quota-to-inode bound in `verbs.rs`.
>   -> From measured concurrency (clients served now, windows a peer's measured rate x RTT), pressure-capped.
> - Device reads: `slates_machine::facts::resident_now` is RSS on macOS, which counts given-back shared pages (above);
>   the pressure hold's own growth reads it. -> The footprint on macOS; Linux PSI and Windows commit already watched
>   (A-570). The pressure seam is consulted by admission only; the sizes above don't read it yet.
> - Give-back on macOS: `MADV_FREE_REUSABLE` over the shared content object leaves RSS (probe: 513 MiB stays, not
>   reclaimed in 10 s under pressure); a purgeable Mach memory entry set `VM_PURGABLE_EMPTY` frees at once (513 -> 1
>   MiB with two mappings), a whole entry at a time. -> Arena extents as purgeable entries handed to the anchor by port.
> - Allocations on the idle path: `prefault_reserve` builds a `Vec` a pass, `purge_keeping` clones the region order,
>   `pieces_against` a `Vec` a run. -> Reused per-shard scratch.
>
> **A lone client's edit and merge after W1 (g222, 2026-11-20; BENCHMARKS, "A lone client after W1 and A-400").**
> W1 had made a single client two to three times slower quiet on every multi-shard daemon (its work on its name's
> shard). **Closed quiet by A-400** (a work on its client's shard): Linux arm64 accept p50 51–55 → 20–21 µs (before W1
> 18), the Mac 155 → 40–43 (before W1 48–54); loaded on Linux main is three times lower than before W1 (p99 21.0 →
> 4.6–7.0 ms). **Open:** (a) about 10 µs added to every quiet lone submit since A-400 (Linux accept p50 20–21 → 31–35
> µs, conflict 17–18 → 27–28; in `f2081a3c8..a5233e228`, bisect under way); (b) the shared Mac loaded, where main is
> still slower than before W1 (accept p50 148–398 against 95–110 µs, p99 9.9–20.2 against 7.8–10.3 ms): the submit's
> ask to the green's owner; (c) the goal's 1 ms loaded p99, met by no arm on either platform.
>
> **A-767 (2026-11-20, w-store; Ada's storage and changeset rulings).** DESIGNED: one unit, the changeset; RAM holds
> the change in flight and a learned cache; history an append-only changeset log on each holder's disk under the
> standing grant; rows (`R N C V O D G`) in Mantle's `ShardDb`; everything else derived. Owed: the log format agreed
> with w-hg, w-git, w-svn; Mantle's crates vendored; `slates-store`; the A/B against per-file deltas; each tool moved
> onto it with an RSS red test.

Part 2 BUILT (A-647): A-614's D(k) and reached sets are a type (`slates-git`'s `store::ReachSets`), each version recording the version its set was remade from; over A-614's generated histories every derived value is the store's own sets and the value it kept, and each derivation walks what its admission walked (`slates-git --lib` 446 of 446). Part 3 BUILT (A-647 part 3, g302, 2026-11-19): the git store keeps each version's two sets as its value alone, put as it commits and held by the version's record, and serves every version's D(k) and reached set from it (an older version's reached set too), the chains' copies dropped; a value names its sets' bytes as an object of any length (format 2), so a set of more runs than one window holds is kept (macOS arm64, Mac Studio, slates-git's store-building modules 185 of 185, slates-server's `vcs_store` 13 and its git service and pushes 14; red first, 5 of 86 failing). Part 4 BUILT (A-647 part 4, g294 from g302's draft, 2026-11-19): each of a version's sets a tree of derived nodes over fixed blocks of positions shaped by the store's window (format 3), so a version's value adds only the nodes on the paths to the blocks its D(k) touches, never its reached set again; over 801 versions of a ref pushed by turns and then merged with 400 older roots in a 256-byte window, the most a version added fell from 7,740 bytes (format 2) to 938 against its bound of 4,352, and 1,077,340 bytes in all to 378,007 (macOS arm64, Mac Studio: red 6 of 7; green slates-git's store-building modules 208 of 208, slates-server's `vcs_store`, git services and pushes 46 of 46, and 52 of 52 as it landed over main 5206419b). Queries by API, part 1 BUILT (A-666, g302, 2026-11-19): `slates-vcs`'s `derived::ancestry`, a type whose value holds Mononoke's commit-graph fields (generation, first-parent and skip-tree skew jumps by Myers' rule, run bottom, skip-tree parent: a dominator), and is-ancestor, the merge bases (git's `--all` set) and bisect's midpoint answered from the values, logarithmic along runs and linear only in the merges a question opens; held to a naive walk over generated histories, to Myers' bound and to the immediate dominator (`research/ancestry-queries.md`). Part 2 BUILT (A-666 part 2, g302, 2026-11-19): `slates-vcs`'s `derived::history`, a type whose value names a version's path map and a history tree of each path's node (Mononoke's unodes), a path keeping the node of the first parent it is TREESAME to (git's default mode exactly; a directory compared by its files, a removal a node), renames and copies as the works recorded them (`PathSources`; a copy from an older version read through `DerivedType::inputs`), and `log <path>` and `--follow` reading at most one node more than the versions they list; held to git's walk over generated histories (`research/path-history.md`; Windows x86_64, jupiter, 65 of 65; the macOS run owed). Part 3 BUILT (A-666 part 3, g302, 2026-11-19): `slates-vcs`'s `derived::blame`, a type whose value keeps each file's blame (runs of lines, each naming its introducing version, the file's path there and its first line there), kept from the first parent whose file holds the same content, else made from the parents' blames, the recorded rename's or copy's source, and one diff with each (Myers' linear-space diff), never a diff of the history; a line both parents of a merge changed attributed by the merge's recorded content (D-27); a question reads the path's trie nodes and the file's spans; held to blame recomputed by replaying every version, each derivation's lines read to the replay's (`research/path-history.md` §6; Windows x86_64, jupiter, 75 of 75; the macOS run owed). OWED: A-553's and A-588's stores as types; the server's use of it; dropping values no version needs; releases and large derivations sliced; merges computed anywhere and committed by position (BUILT, A-658 parts 1 and 2, g305, 2026-11-19: `Green::compute` and `Green::rebase` pure over the versions a work is judged over, a `Computed` holding nothing of the green that computed it and naming its head, typed refusals `BaseUnavailable`/`BaseAhead`, a base past the owner's head no longer judged as if at the head; the owner's `Green::judge_computed` taking a computed verdict by position, judging again only the units whose paths the change index names since or that read the links naming a file one of whose links changed since (A-669, A-670), a content edit from where its ops stood, typed refusals `OtherWork`/`Ahead`/`NotRecorded`, the counter `judged_again`; part 3a BUILT (2026-11-19, g305): a computed verdict's wire form, `Computed::encode` and the owner's `Green::computed_from` against the increment it judged (effects as chain entry records, windows, placements, digest; the oracle takes every held verdict through it); OWED: the fleet's route, a holder computing on its replica and the owner appending (3b); the server's submit and push taking verdicts computed elsewhere (3b, 3c); a rename's edits placed as an edit's are); a blame's spans shared between versions by identity, git's other simplification modes as types, and the server's verbs over A-666's types (each repository's values on its owner shard, A-662; a `PathSources` over each green's versions), with corrected commit dates where a history has them and questions cut into the shard's slices; fetches naming immutable objects through strict tiers; tests at ten times Scion's published numbers.

Part 2 BUILT: the server's driver `crates/server/src/git_push.rs`, one entry point for both edges (`ReceivePack::start`, `input`, `end`, `answer`, each one step on the owner shard): the advertisement of each branch whose green holds a git head (namespace name `N` is `refs/heads/N`, a name beginning `refs/` is itself), a ref the pusher may not read under A-622's policy hidden; input and end over A-638's index view lent the shard's room (`vcs_store::with_room`); a configured git hook refusing every command `hook not run` until A-665 part 2's view; the checked objects admitted to A-662's quarantine and sealed; each command asked of A-622's policy through A-644 part 2's check point (`git_protect`: the right its change needs, then a protected name's linear history and signed commits on what it brings) before its work is built, refused in git's words; A-654 part 1's verdicts over the shard's greens, a ref's base its green's head alone, held at the append by compare and swap; `push_sealed` per entry, or once for all under `atomic`; git's report. Part 3 BUILT: git's HTTP site serves receive-pack through the driver (`vcs_http::git::receive`: each service from its own half, each step lent the state of the shard the connection moved to, a failure before any reply a status, a command's refusal the report's), proven by stock git's `create` push over loopback TLS to a daemon. The SSH site's call BUILT (A-683: `vcs_ssh::receive`, each step lent the shard's state through the HTTP site's seam, `ShardLender`). OWED: the live `git push` over HTTPS and over SSH with stock git's binary (main's runs); the hooks run over A-665 part 2's view (`pre-receive`, `update`, `post-receive`); a push based on an older version than its green's head, refused as a ref that moved until A-664's server-made commits; a principal the policy allows who is not the owner, whom A-635's append refuses `Forbidden`; push options; review requests (`refs/for/`); the new versions' pack fragments encoded off the answer's path (§4.17.2 "A push" item 8); a tag of a tag; a create while the default branch is unborn and holds files no commit names (A-664's).
>
> §4.17.1 maps repositories, branches,
> pushes, stacked changes, review requests, objects and history onto greens and works; §4.17.2 designs the git server;
> §4.17.3 (Mercurial) and §4.17.4 (Subversion) follow as their own amendments. Owed, in order: the seven shared pieces
> of §4.17.1 (the repository record and green ids carrying its partition; one register entry for several greens; the
> object store and its index; works from a client's push, with the head operation and the client-fidelity test; works
> over works and bases given as trees; review records; policy and hooks), then each tool's pieces (§4.17.2's fifteen for
> git, starting with the pkt-line codec). No speed is claimed until main measures it by §4.17.1's and §4.17.2's method.
> **A-515 (2026-11-18):** shared piece 1's first half is built: the repository record and its namespace in the metadata
> database (`crates/db/src/repository.rs`), with its rules model-tested.
> **A-534 (2026-11-19):** shared piece 1's second half is built in the engine. A green's eight current-value maps are

> entries (a key with no history has held its current value since version 0, so a green seeded from its origin no
> longer holds a second copy of the origin's files); and `Lineage::branch` (`crates/merge/src/engine/branch.rs`) makes a
> green at another green's version in O(what changed since that version), O(1) at the head, never a walk. Its oracle
> holds every branch to a green seeded from a copy of its source, over generated histories of every operation kind,
> branches of branches, folds and retires; its walk counter stays still across every branch; red with the reverts, the

> recovered over its source at its version rather than over an origin); the record's replication in a fleet (with

> and its twin are refused, typed, naming their plain SHA-1; and SHA-256 through aws-lc-rs. Golden vectors are every

> its landing are read for the paths the upper names and moved over the lower's operations by the walk the verdict

> Where a work in between does not land in the replica (the verdict depends on order: two inserts at two points and a

> **A-581 (2026-11-19, g083):** shared piece 3's core is built as a pure crate, `crates/vcs` (`slates-vcs`): content by
> BLAKE3 identity, one copy across tools, pushes and repositories, held by count within the owner's derived budget, and
> no content longer than the content plane's window (D-6's chunk, which the owner derives): an object past it is held
> as its windows, cut where a volume cuts the same file, under lists of their identities; lists and tables are named in
> BLAKE3's key-derivation mode, so no pushed bytes are taken for either. Tables of sorted rows of at most a window are
> content, each row naming the contents it holds, opened from any bytes with every fault refused by kind. Each
> repository's index is a tail over runs of tables found by fences; the tail seals its full tables once its rows no
> longer fit one (the table's size and the tail's length derived); a fork holds each table once more (no table written,
> no row copied); the merge point is learned, one rent-or-buy problem for each number of newest runs this index alone
> holds (one rule for every tool, which §4.17.3's and §4.17.4's index rows now read). A push's quarantine checks every
> object by its tool's naming, a parameter that may refuse (git's collision detection), before a byte is stored, and
> is committed as one checked step or abandoned with nothing left. An oracle holds the whole store to plain maps over
> generated histories, and thirteen mutations each turned tests red (`cargo test -p slates-vcs --lib`, 29 of 29, Mac
> Studio; see A-581). Owed: one content index for this store and the volumes' sealed windows (piece 4, Phase 7); a
> merge, a seal, a release and an abandon sliced under the shard's budget; the store and each index on the owner shard,
> timed by its clock, with each tool's naming implemented (each server's object pieces; the Subversion index's rows move
> into these tables there); content-defined cuts of tables and of the large-file class (D-6); pruning what no branch
> reaches; wire-form caches; content placed by identity in a fleet.

> **A-582 part 2 (2026-11-19, g296; protocol v2's messages):** `slates-git` (`v2`) reads and writes the capability
> advertisement, the command request (one `command=` line among the client's capabilities in any order, a delimiter or
> none, a flush alone as the end), `ls-refs`'s arguments and answer, and `fetch`'s seventeen arguments (git's ranges and
> its rules between them) and its response, whose five sections one machine keeps in the document's order for the reader
> and the writer alike (git 2.50.1 wrote wanted-refs first, which its own client refused; git fixed it in
> `191740edaa4a`). Decoding is lossless (each line keeps its LF or its lack, ids are lower-case hexadecimal, numbers
> canonical decimal), so every advertisement, request and answer stock git 2.50.1 wrote or read is written back byte for
> byte; every cut, every bit flip and lines past a packet are refused by kind; admissions are charged exactly first.

> own holders, so a push to one green waits on that green's holders alone. A record is committed once every log it
> moves holds it and every record before it is committed; the committed state is the greatest cut holding every record
> whole, which holders apply at their joins. A replica reads by a vector of positions and refuses one past what it
> applied, a log it holds no copy of, or a split cut. A takeover fences every log's quorum or none and keeps a record
> only where every log's read holds it whole. Tests (Windows x86_64, jupiter; the macOS run owed): red first, the nine

> charged zlib at stock zlib's `compressBound`, which counts stored blocks, while zlib-rs's level 1 (zlib-ng's
> `deflate_quick`) writes every literal in fixed codes and never falls back to one, so bytes that do not compress
> outgrew their charge (65,536 that its fixed codes write in nine bits came to 73,721 against 65,569). zlib's arm is now
> zlib-rs 0.6.8's `compress_bound`, n + ceil(n / 8) + 9, a byte more below 9 bytes and one more for none, which level 1
> meets exactly at 4,095 and 4,096 bytes. Red first on main with the oracle alone

> **Fixed (g083, 2026-11-19, A-691; found by g303 reading `serve/pull.rs`): a hidden draft root was not listed to
> Mercurial peers.** `listkeys phases` answered the draft roots computed over the served view; 7.2's `listphases`
> (`phases.py` 1049-1058) answers the stored draft roots read from the unfiltered changelog, so a draft root an amend
> hid is listed. Reproduced by use with stock 7.2 first (`hg debugpushkey ... phases`, locally and over `hg serve`,
> lists the hidden draft root and its successor; slates' view of the same repository listed the successor alone); now
> `Repository::draft_roots` answers the register's draft roots still draft, read before the served filter; red first
> (r411), green (r421) on macOS arm64, the other platforms owed
> (`docs/bugs/2026-11-19-hg-a-hidden-draft-root-was-not-listed.md`).

> **Fixed (w-interop, 2026-11-20, A-758; found by use, the hg matrix's bookmark-push row): stock hg saw no server key
> but in a clone.** Neither edge listed `pushkey`, so a 7.2 client asked no `listkeys` (`wireprotov1peer.listkeys`
> answers `{}` unasked): `hg incoming -B` and `hg outgoing -B` said "remote doesn't support bookmarks", and `hg
> debugpushkey` listed nothing. Now `pushkey` is listed over SSH and HTTP and its command served, landed as a push of
> one advisory `pushkey` part through the one push driver (`slates_hg::serve::keys`; heads `force`; the policy, hooks
> and race checks a part's key meets), answered `1` or `0` with words; a namespace no key is moved in (`obsolete`, any
> other) is refused by type before anything lands, answered `0` naming it. Red first and green by use with stock 7.2
> over both edges (`hg_interop`'s `stock_hg_lists_and_moves_keys_over_the_*_edge`) on macOS arm64; other platforms
> owed. A `pushkey` inside a `batch` (w-interop, 2026-11-20) is landed between its neighbours as a lone one is
> (`serve::session::Batch`: the calls answered in order, a later `listkeys` reading the move); over HTTP only by `POST`,
> as 7.2 checks a batched call's `push` permission, so stock hg's batch by `GET` (sent so to any server not listing
> `httppostargs`, slates included) is refused `405` as a stock server refuses it. Red first by use (`command not served
> here` over both edges), green: `hg_interop`'s `stock_hg_batches_a_pushkey_over_the_*_edge`, the edge's
> `a_batched_pushkey_is_landed_over_post_and_refused_over_get`, the session's `a_batched_pushkey_is_landed_between_its_
> neighbours`.

> **Fixed (g083, 2026-11-19, A-690; found by g303 reading `serve/pull.rs`): divergent bookmarks were listed to
> Mercurial peers.** `serve::pull::bookmark_entries`, which `listkeys bookmarks` and a `getbundle`'s `bookmarks` part
> read, listed every bookmark naming a held changeset; 7.2's `listbinbookmarks` (`bookmarks.py` 475-484) leaves out a
> divergent name (`isdivergent`, 471-472: an `@` not as its last byte). Reproduced by use with stock 7.2 first (a
> bookmark diverged in a clone and pulled back: `hg serve` answers `@` and `feature`, slates' view of the same
> repository answered `feature@1` too); now the rule is `crate::bookmarks::divergent`, shared with the push's refusal;
> red first (r340), green (r356) on macOS arm64, the other platforms owed
> (`docs/bugs/2026-11-19-hg-divergent-bookmarks-were-listed-to-peers.md`).

> **Fixed (g300, 2026-11-19, A-667; found by g304 against stock 7.2): Mercurial's branch heads were judged by a child on
> the branch.** `serve::discovery::branch_head_revs` took a revision for its branch's head when no child of it was on
> its branch; 7.2's rule (`branchmap.py` 422-424) ends every revision a later one on its branch descends from, through
> any branches, so `default` 0, `stable` 1, `default` 2 answered `default`'s heads 0 and 2 where 7.2 answers 2, in
> `branchmap` and `check:updated-heads`. A-619's and A-641's oracles stated the same rule, so they certified it. Now the
> rule is 7.2's, a branch walked only where its candidates have children on other branches and a parent from another
> branch lies above them, closed heads kept; red first (6 failed), then 284 of 284 on Windows x86_64 (jupiter), macOS
> owed (`docs/bugs/2026-11-19-hg-branch-heads-were-judged-by-a-child-on-the-branch.md`). Apart from 7.2 on purpose: a
> merge whose parent on its branch is an ancestor of its other parent, where 7.2 keeps a head by its cache's history.
> Owed: an obsolete changeset the served view shows is never a head in 7.2; the view carries no obsolescence yet.

> **Fixed (g267, 2026-11-19, A-577; found settling A-565): a live clone was answered before any of it was durable.** A
> clone of a live-shipped volume is live-shipped too, but its `Clone` reply waited on its origin's log, and its record,
> a copy of its origin's, named the origin's head, so nothing of it shipped until its own first seal: at `f = 1` an owner
> lost before the clone's first write was durable left a successor with no log and no seal of it, an acknowledged clone
> lost, its status reading a zero window; at `f > 0` its writes waited until the held-reply bound refused them; and
> its log's whole records were its recovery image, which names its inherited tree by number, so a rebuild from the log
> found no root to lay out. Now a clone's registers start at the creation head (the fleet knows it at once), a live
> log's whole records stand alone (`Volume::to_standalone_image`; a later full record's shared inodes kept from the
> image before it, `live_ship::keep_shared`), its reply waits for its own first whole entry durable on `f` holders
> (after its alias on the cross-partition path), and its status reports the window its seals leave until its new log has
> answered at a whole entry. The reply's cost: one entry, the clone's whole image,
> answered at one round trip to `f` holders, behind the record plane's placement of its catalog and creation head (up to
> two record periods for a clone the fleet does not know yet). **Owed:** an image merged as a clone
> (`image::run_merge`) still answers before its live clone's log holds it; the record plane shipping a new live volume's
> catalog and creation head on demand rather than at its period; the fleet's own test of the window (filed for main).
> Record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-19-a-live-clone-is-answered-before-any-of-it-is-durable.md`.

> **Open (A-510, 2026-11-18): kiln saw a Slates instance serve on for two minutes after a fire-and-exit `SIGTERM`; Slates'
> own stop does not wait on the sender.** kiln's K5 real-instance test (g267, kiln r407, the Mac Studio) sent its anchor
> `SIGTERM` and returned, and the instance was seen serving about two minutes later. Waiting for the stop (r443, r457)
> it ended in 204 ms and 176 ms. Slates' stop path waits on nothing the sender holds. Its lines never panic on a closed
> pipe. The anchor leads its own process group. The anchor ends any stop within its own bounds (`stop_step`,
> `stop_overdue`). The daemon's stop asks no client anything. The guard test
> `an_anchor_whose_stop_was_asked_by_a_sender_that_exited_stops_within_its_bound` (`crates/api/src/role/stop_tests.rs`)
> has a sender that starts the anchor in its own group, holds a written write attachment, sends `SIGTERM` and exits at
> once. There the anchor and daemon were gone in 191 ms (283 ms with a bare client). Not reproduced, so not fixed: what
> kiln's run had beyond it is the anchor as kiln's executable, the launcher's secret on standard input, a log file, the
> K5 scenario's captured clones, the test's temporary directory removed right after the signal (with the clones'
> base), and kiln's runner's handling of leftover processes. **Owed:** kiln's K5 in its fire-and-exit shape, the
> anchor's log kept outside the temporary directory, with `ps` states and a `sample` of the anchor and daemon during the
> two minutes (filed for main). Record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-18-a-stop-asked-by-a-sender-that-exited.md`.

> **The fenced register's invariants over the real holders, under a network nemesis: built (2026-11-18, goal 81's chaos
> part, its network half, g229).** The register invariants TLC proved over `FencedRegister.tla` and `FencedLedger.tla`
> were never checked over the implementation as history checks. `crates/db/src/register_nemesis.rs` (lib tests) runs the
> real `Acceptor` and the owner's rules over a simulated network, under latency and reordering, loss, duplication,
> one-way and two-way cuts, holders knocked offline and back from their persisted state, owners paused and resumed,
> takeovers, and owner restarts under one generation. It checks Agreement (TotalOrder), Continuity (NoLoss for a
> register), StaleNeverCommits and ReadSafety after every accept, commit and adoption. 48 seeds each at `f = 1` and
> `f = 2` (1,500 steps a seed) break none, with every fault and the stale and late cases counted (the Mac Studio, 9 s
> for all four tests). Three mutations kept as tests each break histories (a promise without its fence 39/48 and 44/48;
> a restart that forgets the fence 16/192 and 9/192; promotion on a minority 23/48 and 7/48), and ReadSafety has a
> direct red check. Found: the fence carries the load only across an owner's restart under one generation; a takeover's
> generation refuses the stale owner first. **The live log's half: built (2026-11-19, A-601).**
> `crates/db/tests/live.rs` now judges ReadSafety too, beside Agreement, NoLoss, StaleNeverCommits and Convergence:
> every read phase one could make were the current owner lost adopts a state holding every durable write, judged after
> every step and every settling delivery (the Mac Studio, kiln r176: 7,198 and 6,329 reads judged at `f = 1` and
> `f = 2`, 3,721 and 3,035 of them past a holder without a durable write, none broken). Its first run found the model's
> successor naming fresh members as holders without `following`, which the daemon's does not; the model now takes the
> superseded shipper's committed holders. The daemon's question it raised is answered by reading (A-601, continued
> (1)): a live-shipped volume can be taken over with no holders recorded, but then no log ever shipped, no holder is
> counted, the volume is served from its placed seal, and the successor's configuration-chosen holders belong to a
> log that begins new; a successor of an adopted log keeps the recorded holders (`live_ship`'s module doc). **Owed:**
> the real-process runs of `crates/cli/tests/live_chaos.rs` (main's).

> **A holder behind its own records answered every later version out of order: fixed (2026-11-18, A-412, §4.16 "Apply on
> holders"; g250; the bug record of the same day).** A takeover commits the versions it adopted again through the
> register path, which carries no inputs, and the record plane never ships a placed version again, so a holder whose
> replica had not reached them held their records and could not apply them: it answered every later version
> `merge.out_of_order` for good, and at `f = 1` with the old owner gone the successor's next version never placed. Now a
> record ahead of the replica finds the versions between in the holder's own ledger: their inputs held, the replica
> advances through them and the record is served as its next; an input not held is fetched by identity from the
> record's owner (`fleet::fetch_ledger_inputs`, `merge.catch_up.begun`, `merge.catch_up.fetched`). Test:
> `a_holder_behind_its_own_records_after_a_takeover_fetches_their_inputs_and_takes_the_next_version`
> (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`): green in 4.4 s (kiln r355, Mac Studio, debug); red without the catch-up, version 4
> answered out of order 4,865 times in 405 s and never placed.
> - **Open (sibling):** a holder restarted warm with no replica, holding a record whose input it lacks, rebuilds nothing
>   (the A-313 rebuild meets the missing input) and nothing fetches the input.

> **A takeover's successor answered a forwarded read `NotFound` before it had made the volume: fixed (2026-11-18, A-394,
> ReadSafety, §4.8 "Lookup"; g250; the chaos nemesis, seed 6876545201569229162 on macOS).** With A-382 in, the seed's
> fourteen faults all recovered on the Mac Studio, and the verdict failed ReadSafety alone, 3 of 3 runs: during the first
> fault (the owner isolated), five reads through a holder of the newest acknowledged writes answered "missing". A
> diagnostic build (kiln r251) logged each: the holder's routing named the takeover's successor as the owner, the holder
> forwarded the reads there, and the successor, owning the volume by its own routing but not yet holding it in its
> catalog, served each as any forwarded verb is served, found no volume and answered `NotFound`: a claim that the file
> did not exist. A forwarded write met the same `NotFound` and had it recorded as its completion. A local client's verb
> there already met `owned_unmaterialized`'s retryable `Overloaded`; a forwarded one now meets the same
> (`verbs::forwarded_before_made`, counted `fleet.forward.refused.before_made`), before any completion is recorded.
> Test: `a_forwarded_read_of_a_volume_owned_here_but_not_made_is_refused_retryably` (`crates/server/src/verbs.rs`), red
> without the guard (`NotFound`). The seed on the fix (kiln r264, Mac Studio, debug build): 2 of 2 runs pass, every
> invariant held, 91.9 s and 63.5 s; on main bf58691 without it (r212), 3 of 3 failed ReadSafety alone, five reads each.
> **Owed (the supervisor's):** the seed on both Linux arches on the fix.

> **A volume whose owner shard refused its state read as absent: fixed (2026-11-19, A-564, §4.8 "Lookup"; g225; found by
> A-557).** A verb forwarded to its volume's owner shard was answered `NotFound` whenever the owner did not run it:
> - from another node, `serve_forward` took `xshard::call_in_shard_time`'s `None` (not sent, given up, or the owner's
>   borrow refused), and `named_if_unshared` turned it into `NotFound`;
> - on the same node, `send_forward`'s task turned a refused owner borrow into `NotFound`.
>
> So a volume on a fenced owner (a failed consensus publication) read as absent. The owner's refusal is now answered by
> its kind:
> - a fenced owner, or a retention check that fences it, answers `ConsensusRecoveryUnavailable`, the refusal a failed
>   publication answers;
> - a call that did not run answers `Overloaded`, not started.
>
> `PromoteRegion` and the partition lookup on a refused control shard are answered the same way, and so is a deferred
> write's completion poll. Test: `a_verb_for_a_volume_whose_owner_is_fenced_is_refused_by_the_fence_never_not_found`
> (`crates/server/src/verbs.rs`), red before with `NotFound`. Record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-11-19-a-volume-on-a-fenced-owner-read-as-absent.md`.

> **A host admitted again refused its successor's records for good, so its live copy never caught up: fixed
> (2026-11-18, A-382, §4.8 "Authority scope"; g230; the chaos nemesis's convergence, seeds 6876545201569229162 and
> 7236833171758868842 on arm64, CI diag 44345243646).** The superseded adopter, admitted again under its id, kept its
> register copies of the objects it had adopted under its own authority, at their old generation: its re-admission
> forgot its own routes, and the install moves a copy only along its route. So it refused the creator's catalog and
> head `ForeignGeneration` every period (660 to 796 a run), and the creator, which ships a live log only to a holder
> holding its catalog, never sent it the log: its live copy stayed at fence 2 behind the creator's fence 3 for a whole
> fleet wait. Fixed: the re-admission lets those copies go (`readmission::let_go_own_registers`,
> `fleet.readmission.registers_let_go`), so the successor's next record makes them afresh, and a volume a node lost to
> a successor ships no catalog or head record (`fleet::unplaced_heads`). Tests:
> `every_copy_catches_up_once_the_creator_takes_its_volume_back_from_the_adopter`,
> `every_copy_catches_up_once_the_third_node_takes_the_volume_from_the_adopter` and
> `a_superseded_owner_restarted_warm_ships_no_record_of_the_volume_it_lost` (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`). Bug
> record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-18-a-readmitted-adopters-own-register-copies-refused-its-successor-for-good.md`.
> - **Not this entry: the x86_64 runs of the same seeds** ended two daemons each by their watchdogs ("shard N is
>   spinning, 1000 ms of CPU without a step") right after the supersession, so the dead nodes' copies read none: the
>   live takeover's materialization in one turn, g251's item, as seed 17036665960917068132.
> - **Fixed (A-409, 2026-11-18): a superseded owner's shipper that was never told its fence shipped on.** In 2 of 12
>   runs of the third node's case (CI diag 44358084443) the re-admitted adopter's own log of the volume, yielded but
>   never fenced, built 119 and 1,714 installs for the creator, which refused each `not_the_acting_owner`. Now a yielded
>   volume's log ships nothing and does no period work, as a fenced one (A-349), its waiting verbs answered
>   `DurabilityPending` at the yield (`live_ship::yielded`, counted `fleet.live.yield_refused`); and a holder refusing a
>   stale sender tells it the highest fence it knows, its record copy's as well as its live copy's
>   (`live_ship::known_fence`), so a sender below it is fenced. Why no refusal fenced it in that run is not read from
>   its counters (the creator's live copy showed fence 3 against the adopter's 2 at the end); the run that shows the
>   storm gone is filed for main (run-requests.md).
> - **Fixed (A-415): the let-go is published at once.** The re-admission publishes the shard right after it lets the
>   copies go (`readmission::let_go_own_registers`; a refused publication is counted
>   `fleet.readmission.registers_let_go_unpublished` and the next carries it), so a warm restart no longer restores
>   them naming this host. **Still owed:** the yield itself is memory-only (`ShardState::yielded`), so a warm restart
>   forgets that the node lost the volume at all (A-334).
> - **Owed: a copy made afresh takes the first member's record at the current generation as its owner's,** as a new
>   candidate's does. A node that knows it lost a volume (yielded or fenced) ships it no record; a stale owner that
>   does not know yet was retired, so it is no member until its re-admission yields.

> **Partly closed (g262, 2026-11-18): every wire enum of the protocol and of the records is held to its published
> tags by a test.** Two guards read each wire enum's schema, which names its variants in tag order:
> `crates/ipc/tests/wire_order.rs` (43 enums, 410 tags) and `crates/db/tests/wire_order.rs` (17 enums, 152 tags, `Op`
> among them). Each compares its enums with its `tests/wire_order.txt`, and both share
> `crates/ipc/tests/support/wire_order.rs`. A second test in each fails when the crate's sources derive `Wire` for an
> enum the guard does not hold. An append is published in its change by the `--ignored` writer
> (`publish_appended_variants`), which refuses while any published tag moved. `SubmitApproved` stays at 71: moving it
> back would be a second move, and builds since 04d7ea465 speak 71. Still owed, from the entry below: the completion
> record framed with its reply's schema hash (the log's owner).

> **Open (g267, 2026-11-18): the wire's append-only rule (D-15) is kept by review alone, and a persisted reply is read
> outside every schema check.** A variant's wire tag is its index in its enum (`crates/wire-derive/src/lib.rs`,
> `expand_enum`). 04d7ea465 (A-285) inserted `RequestBody::SubmitHeld` and `EditSubmitHeld` before `SubmitApproved`, so
> `SubmitApproved`'s tag moved from 69 to 71 (`CONTRACT` 6 had published it). Nothing was misread: a ring or fleet frame
> carries its body's schema hash (`protocol::frame`), so a client and a daemon of different builds refuse each other
> whole, and no request body is kept. A reply is: a completion record keeps `ReplyBody` unframed
> (`CompletionRecord::result`, recorded by `Op::CompletionRecorded` and read back by `ReplyBody::from_bytes` in
> `crates/server/src/verbs.rs`), and the log's own schema hash covers that field only as bytes. So the same insertion in
> `ReplyBody`, or in any type it carries (`Refusal`, `MoveRefusal`, ...), would have a daemon restarted on a newer build
> over the anchor's segment answer a retried request with another reply than the one it recorded, or `DuplicateRequest`.
> Owed: a structural check that every enum the wire or a record carries only grows at its end (a golden of its variants
> in order, its regeneration behind `--ignored`), and the completion record framed with its reply's schema hash, so a
> record of another schema is refused typed rather than read as another reply. g262 (the contract's owner) told.

> **A learner, the pair's lower anchor, dropped a voter that kept it, and the pair's probe mesh never formed: fixed
> (2026-11-18, A-337, §4.8; goal g225).** `a_learners_reports_reach_the_council_once_the_voter_it_joined_from_is_gone`
> failed its fixture's formation wait once in g251's diag run 44262759484 (ubuntu, 2026-11-18; 49 to 50 periods after the
> initial consensus settled in 0.83 s): voter c kept learner e (`AsVoter`), e dropped c (`OutsideNeighbourhood`), and e
> was the pair's lower anchor, the only side whose dial keys the pair's plane. The role rule is kept from both sides
> only while both read the same voters, and a learner's can be stale. Fixed: the pair's canonical dialer keeps a peer
> that holds a record session it dialed to it (`DirectContact::Dialed`, `ShardState::dialed_in`). Test:
> `the_pairs_canonical_dialer_keeps_a_peer_that_dialed_it_and_only_it` (`crates/server/src/daemon.rs`). Bug record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-11-18-a-learner-the-pairs-lower-anchor-dropped-a-voter-that-kept-it.md`.
> - **Fixed (2026-11-18, A-380): a learner's voters are versioned.** A seat change was a Raft configuration entry that
>   moved no configuration version, so a learner never fetched on it, and a learner answered by another learner took that
>   one's known voters (`a_learner_learns_who_votes_once_the_voter_it_joined_from_is_gone`: 3 of 24 runs at one CPU, a
>   learner naming only the stopped bootstrapper). Now the configuration records the council's voters, the leader
>   records the voters in force once no change is in flight (`ConfigCommand::Seat`), and a learner reads them from the
>   configuration it holds. Tests: `a_learner_names_the_voters_the_configuration_records_through_a_seat_change`
>   (`crates/cluster/src/config_group.rs`), `a_seat_records_the_voters_in_id_order_and_advances_the_version_only_when_they_change`
>   (`crates/db/src/register.rs`), the round trip in `crates/cluster/src/raft_wire.rs`. The root group's learners named
>   the root voters of their join (the open sibling of the 2026-11-08 entry) until A-406 recorded the root voters the
>   same way (`RootCommand::Seat`; a root learner also fetches once a root voter it knows is no longer alive). Test:
>   `a_root_learner_names_the_voters_the_configuration_records_through_a_seat_change`
>   (`crates/cluster/src/root_group.rs`).
> - **Owed (the supervisor's):** the learner tests' rate on the diag lanes once this lands
>   (`a_learners_reports_reach_the_council_once_the_voter_it_joined_from_is_gone` and its three siblings, at one CPU
>   beside two busy loops, as diag-g225-forming-fleet-reaches-2 ran them).

> **"Initial membership did not commit": the bootstrapper's record dial to one peer sat in its first handshake call for
> 10.8 to 15.8 s, so its council or root could not stage that peer (open, 2026-11-18, §4.8; goal g225).** Three
> formations failed this way, each at `settle_initial_consensus` (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`): the Mac Studio (macOS
> arm64, `a_placed_snapshot_is_held_whole_by_f_plus_one_hosts_of_the_mirror_region` under background QoS, 1 of 688 runs,
> kiln r156), and GitHub's diag-g225-forming-fleet-reaches-3 (run 44346317178, one CPU beside two busy loops, 2 of about
> 8,000 runs: `a_root_learner_fetches_the_committed_region_membership_over_the_transport` on ubuntu-latest,
> `a_campaign_waits_for_a_voters_session_that_is_out_for_a_moment` on ubuntu-24.04-arm). In each, the bootstrapper (the
> council or root leader) reported for one peer `RecordDialReport { dialing_for_ns: Some(t), call_for_ns: Some(t),
> budgets_spent: 0, stall: None, calls: 1 }` with t 15.8, 12.9 and 10.8 s, and no `fleet.dial.*` count, while that peer
> held a record session to the bootstrapper. That peer's demultiplexer had opened one session fewer than every other
> node's and replaced one fewer (a healthy node's shows two opens and one replacement for each peer, read here as the
> seed dial and the dial under the learned id): no second session from the bootstrapper was ever opened. The leader's
> staging of that member never caught up with no session to replicate over (`RaftNode::catch_up`), so its voter change
> never began, and the formation wait gave up after 10.8 to 14.2 s. A dialer keeps its socket for two handshake budgets
> of 33 probe timeouts each (`ESTABLISH_BUDGETS_BEFORE_REDIAL`, `handshake_deadline`, about 44 s) before it dials from a
> new port, longer than a formation. Not yet known: whether the second call resends on the seed dial's socket into a
> session the peer no longer answers, sends nowhere, or is never woken. The instrumented branch
> `agents/g225-diag-formation-4` logs every record dial's addresses and end, every session a demultiplexer opens, every
> handshake datagram that reaches an established session, and a dialer's silent retransmits; it did not fail in 2,417
> runs on the Mac Studio (kiln r208), and its run is filed for main (`~/.cache/slates-scratch/fanout/run-requests.md`,
> 2026-11-18T19:20Z g225). The other two shapes of this failure are distinct: a leader whose follower holds a joint
> entry the leader lacks (the integrator's diag-green-44269355181 arm64 run 7: leader at last log 6, follower at 7, same
> term 1, no stuck dial), and the Windows two-region root whose new voters reported no committed root voter set (run
> 44298844583, no stuck dial).
