> **A volume reported no loss window: built (2026-11-17, AC-8.3, §4.10 "Auto-seal"; g230).** Nothing told an agent
> what an owner loss would cost it, or a successor's client what one had cost: the status promised
> `last_placed_snapshot_age` and carried nothing. `status` now carries `LossReport`: `at_risk_ns` (zero at a placed,
> unchanged head or a live-shipped volume in a fleet; the newest placed seal's age otherwise; the volume's age with
> none placed, always on a laptop), `placed_sequence` (that seal's head sequence) and, on a successor, `taken_over`
> (epoch, head sequence served from, from the live log or not); a consumer reads it through slates-api
> (`VolumeStatus::loss`, CONTRACT 10). Test:
> `a_successor_reports_the_loss_window_its_takeover_left` (`crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`; a second seal kept from
> placing by refusing the owner's records, so the window is the edits after the last *placed* seal, not the last seal).
> - **Owed:** auto-seal at a derived cadence (Phase 8 task 8), which bounds the window; it needs the operator's
>   loss-window SLO, a decision for Ada (options in the g230 progress record).
> - **Closed (2026-11-18, A-325):** the takeover report survives the successor's restart: it is kept in the volume's
>   record (`VolumeRecord::taken_over`). The test found that the volume itself did not: nothing published the shard's
>   image after a takeover until the volume's first write, so a successor restarted before then refused it `NoImage`
>   and never served it again. A volume taken over from its seal is now published before it is served. Test:
>   `a_successors_takeover_report_survives_its_warm_restart`.
> - **Closed (2026-11-18, A-343):** a live-shipped volume taken over is published at its takeover too, so a successor
>   restarted before its first write keeps it. Test: `a_successor_restarted_before_any_write_keeps_the_live_volume_it_took_over`.

> **A sealed envelope's wrap and open were quadratic in its chunks: linear (2026-11-17, A-92 piece 3b; g230).** The
> wrap (`slates_cluster::envelope::wrap`) checked each sealed chunk against every chunk already stored, and the open
> found each entry's chunk by a scan: `n²` identity comparisons each, about 1.3e8 for a 1 GiB volume of 64 KiB chunks,
> the open on a takeover's path (the recovery budget is 1 s) and the wrap in one turn of the owner shard. Now a set and
> an index. Test: `an_envelope_of_thousands_of_chunks_opens_to_the_very_archive` (`crates/cluster/tests/envelope.rs`).
> **Owed (measurement, the supervisor's):** `cargo run --release -p slates-cluster --example envelope_bench` at 16,384
> chunks, before and after. The wrap's one owner-shard turn at a seal's end is in turns since A-323 (2026-11-18, above).

> **The seal walk held its shard for every seal at once: in turns (2026-11-17, §4.10 "Content replication", CLAUDE.md
> "Bounded work everywhere"; g230, the sibling of the live period's slicing below).** Each record period the owner
> shard's seal walk (`fleet::advance_seals`, and `advance_mirror_seals` for a mirror) visited every volume in one turn
> and advanced every seal job's archive a slice, each slice sized to the shard's step quantum: `n` volumes sealing at
> once held the shard's clients for `n` quanta. It now runs in turns of about a step quantum
> (`fleet::seal_walk_slice`, counted `fleet.seal.walk_slices` against `fleet.seal.walks`), each turn's content puts
> dispatched before the next. Test: `a_shards_seals_are_walked_in_turns_and_every_one_places` (the turn injected to one
> volume, `Daemon::inject_seal_walk_quantum`). **Owed:** the owner shard's longest step with hundreds of volumes sealing
> at once (measurement, the supervisor's). The envelope wrap at a seal's end, one turn of the whole archive then, is in
> turns since A-323 (2026-11-18, above).

> **owner_turn's refused `mkdir` asked the program, not the kernel: fixed (2026-11-18, test only).**
> `a_mutations_reply_waits_for_its_barrier_and_a_refused_barrier_answers_eio` (`crates/bridge-fuse/tests/owner_turn.rs`)
> failed on every CI run of the ubuntu-latest gates job since main moved to Ubuntu 26.04 (from run 43146258837 on
> 2026-11-12 to 44210937388 on 2026-11-18; diag-slabs-58 200 of 200 alone), and was ledgered as a rare race. It is
> not a race: 26.04's `/usr/bin/mkdir` is uutils coreutils 0.10.0, which is told `EIO` by `mkdir(2)` and exits 0
> because the refused directory exists in the volume (strace in diag-slabs-61, run 43146145846). The owner refused the
> right request (`MkDir`) and the kernel answered `EIO`. The test now makes the directory by `mkdir(2)` and holds the
> answer to `EIO`. Swept: no other test judges a coreutils program's refusal through a mount (the rest redirect in the
> shell, `cat` a missing path, or run util-linux's `fallocate`). **Consequence, open:** the job runs `cargo test
> --workspace`, which stops at the first failing binary, so no suite after `slates-bridge-fuse`'s `owner_turn` ran on
> that lane from 2026-11-12 until this fix; the first run with it is the stack that lands it. Record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-11-18-owner-turns-mkdir-asked-the-program-not-the-kernel.md`.

> **KIND on Ubuntu 26.04 ran out of inotify instances: fixed in the lane (2026-11-09).** The KIND lane failed at
> formation on `ubuntu-latest` once it became 26.04 (`peers_probed=0`), and passed on 24.04. The image keeps the
> kernel's `fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 128` (24.04's set 1280), which kind's six privileged nodes share as the
> host's root; kube-proxy crash-looped on 4 of 5 workers, so pods there never reached the cluster's DNS. Raised to
> kind's documented 512 (and 524288 watches), 6 of 6 kube-proxies ran with 0 restarts (diag-release-14). The job
> raises them before the lane; the image stays 26.04. Record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-11-09-kind-on-ubuntu-26-04-ran-out-of-inotify-instances.md`.

> **Device nodes are kept as metadata (2026-11-17, §4.5, §4.6, §4.15, §4.16; A-294, Ada's option (c) for A-26 of
> 2026-11-18; replaces A-268's `EPERM`).** A block or character device node is now an inode whose body is its number,
> kept through the volume, its recovery image (28) and delta (11), archives (manifest minor 4), merges and ext4 images,
> and made and reported by FUSE (`rdev`) and NFS (`rdev`, NFSv4 `rawdev`) with its number. Linux's rule decides who
> makes one: root, except a whiteout (a character device 0/0) for any caller who may write the directory. Nothing opens
> one as a device: a landing refuses it before its first write, and each consumer's kernel is guarded (slates' own
> mounts `nosuid,nodev`, the Linux FUSE mount now stating both itself; a pod's device cgroup; a guest asked for
> `nosuid,nodev`, a real guest's test of both built 2026-11-18, A-94's amendment). Proven by each crate's unit tests
> (A-294 names them). **Owed:**
> - ~~every root pjdfstest list re-recorded with its record from a real run (the integrator's lanes)~~ **done
>   2026-11-18.** Every device-fixture entry passed where predicted: CI run 44252249999 (virtio-fs guest 1,798 of
>   1,798; macOS NFS 1,788 of 1,905) and run 44258878562 (the Linux FUSE adapter 1,798 of 1,800). Each list shrank by
>   exactly those cases (virtio-fs, NFSv4 and OCI to none). The three Linux lanes' records were re-recorded by diag run
>   44262117526, which met every verdict over the shrunk lists (FUSE 2 expected failures, NFSv4 and OCI none, 8,770 of
>   8,798 passed), and `docs/wip/conformance.md` was regenerated from them;
> - the real-kernel tests run on the Linux lanes: `a_device_node_reaches_the_mount_with_its_number_and_is_never_opened`
>   (FUSE) and `a_device_node_is_made_with_its_number_and_never_opened` (the NFSv4 kernel client, which now mounts
>   `nosuid,nodev`);
> - the KIND lane's first run of its device probe (`device_probe` in `xtask/src/kind_export.rs`, written with this
>   change): a root pod makes `/dev/null`'s and `/dev/mem`'s numbers in the volume, and an unprivileged pod must open
>   the first (the control: the pod's bind is not `nodev`) and be refused `EPERM` on the second by the device cgroup;
> - the first runs of a guest's proof over virtio-fs, built 2026-11-18 (A-94's amendment, kiln goal g260):
>   `a_guests_mount_of_slates_own_device_runs_no_set_id_file_as_its_owner_and_opens_no_device_node` in
>   `crates/cli/tests/guest_vhost.rs`. The guest mounts the tag `nosuid,nodev`, as the guest mount line in `docs/cli.md`
>   asks since 2026-11-17. The test expects a whiteout the host's user makes to be refused `EACCES` there and to reach
>   the device layer (`ENXIO`) through a control mount without the flags, and a set-id copy of the probe to run as its
>   caller there and as its owner through the control. Not yet run in a guest: CI's live-guest lane runs it in QEMU
>   11.1, and the supervisor's run is crosvm on adacachy;
> - Windows: a device node (and a FIFO or socket) has no WinFsp form. A directory holding one failed its whole listing
>   (`read_all_entries` took each entry's attribute word with `?`), a sibling defect since A-26 that kept device nodes
>   make common (an unpacked `/dev`); fixed 2026-11-17, the drive's listing leaves such an entry out (`listed`), so a
>   directory holding only such entries lists empty and its removal is refused `STATUS_DIRECTORY_NOT_EMPTY`; the live
>   proof is owed to CI's Windows runner. Showing them in WSL's form, a reparse point tagged `IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_CHR`,
>   `_LX_BLK`, `_LX_FIFO` or `_AF_UNIX`, is the candidate, now that the drive answers reparse requests (A-275).

> **A snapshot's attribute-only change was lost in recovery: fixed (2026-11-17, §4.8).** The image's cross-snapshot
> dedup matched a version to an earlier snapshot's by its body alone, while the rebuild shares the earlier snapshot's
> whole record, so a version changed only by a `chmod`, `chown` or `touch` between two snapshots recovered with the
> earlier one's metadata (snapshot `b` read 0o644 for its 0o600, `a_version_that_differs_only_in_its_attributes_keeps_them_through_recovery`).
> Every FIFO, socket and device-node version shares one body, so for them any two versions matched. The match now
> needs the whole inode image equal. Record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-17-a-snapshots-attribute-only-change-was-lost-in-recovery.md`.

> **A lone daemon's end left the line's writer unjoined: fixed (2026-11-18, A-232).** Main's TSan lane failed both
> stuck-shard tests of `crates/client/tests/lone_daemon.rs` from the push that landed A-232 (run 44210937388): "the lone
> daemon was still running 10s after its shard was held". The watchdog reached its verdict within a window and logged
> its end every time (diag-g218-tsan-1, run 44216526894, 3 of 3 runs); the exit then ran ThreadSanitizer's finalizer,
> which sleeps a second (`atexit_sleep_ms`) and reported the end's writer thread, finished and never joined, as a leak.
> Symbolizing the report held the exit 26.3-26.8 s, and the process exited 66, ThreadSanitizer's code for a reported
> warning, not 4 (diag-g218-tsan-2, run 44217144677). With `atexit_sleep_ms=0` the writer was still running at the
> exit, so nothing was reported and both tests passed with exit 4. Uninstrumented, the tests passed 3 of 3. The end
> (`watchdog::end_process`) now joins the writer once it says the line is written; a writer blocked past a beat is
> still ended by the exit, as A-232 decided. Swept: no other production `process::exit` follows a spawned thread.
> Record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-18-the-watchdogs-end-left-its-writer-unjoined.md`.

> **Closed, measured and rejected (A-528, 2026-11-19; opened by g222, 2026-11-17, A-273): rebases and named-version
> reads of a green on the shards holding its works.** Built whole (steps 1 to 4, 5a and 5b, A-473 and A-502), lost the
> 1,000-client A/B twice (r406 and r100), and removed whole by A-528 with no flag and no dormant path: a work's rebase
> and base reads are the owner's again (BENCHMARKS, "A green's replicas on the shards that hold its works: measured and
> rejected"). The record of what was built: The owner spends 51–53% of its wall on verdicts and rebases at the 3,000-client rung (W1),
> rebases the larger share (about 71,000 a run against 49,000 verdicts), and W1's rebase at 1,000 clients is slower
> than main's because it crosses to the owner. A replica holds the green's metadata (about 14.2 MB at the rung, 3.8% of
> a shard's 373.5 MB metadata budget on the Studio) and reads the owner's content in place, never a copy (the
> supervisor, 2026-11-17, by A-64 and D-7). W1 is on main (3c0af9399). **Built (step 1):** the owner's frees held until
> every replica has acknowledged the feed position that released them (positions, since a fold releases with no new
> version), charged to the green's retained bytes and counted (`Green::hold_content`, `acknowledge_content`,
> `leave_content`, `content_frees_held`; tests in `crates/merge/src/history.rs`). **Built (step 2, 2026-11-18,
> g083):** the replica and its feed (`crates/merge/src/replica.rs`): built from the owner's checkpoint at its head and
> its feed position, fed each committed version and each fold in order, a gap or a version that would replay as
> another refused unchanged and the replica rebuilt, counted; equal to the owner at every version over generated
> histories with messages late, lost or in flight across a rebuild (`crates/merge/tests/replica.rs`). **Built (step 3,
> 2026-11-18, g083):** the green's content in sealed blocks (`slates_mem::sealed`), current files and history chunks
> alike: a replica is made from the owner whole and reads the owner's blocks in place, holding no content of its own
> (its current bytes are the owner's memory, by pointer, in the oracle); its replay adopts the owner's blocks in order,
> checked byte for byte; the owner frees a released block once every replica has passed its release. A replica's
> lifetime is bounded by its owner's: the owner's holder makes every replica leave before it gives the owner up
> (`SealedBlocks::end`), and an owner dropped with one still registered frees nothing and is counted (Miri found a
> test that never made its reader leave; the bug record of 2026-11-18). **Built (step 4, 2026-11-18, g083):** the
> bounds, each derived from the machine by a stated formula (`crates/merge/src/replica.rs`) and each a typed refusal
> after which the replica is rebuilt from the owner or given back, its work going to the owner: the replicas an owner
> takes, `replica_limit` = (shards − 1) × 2, none with one shard (`ReplicaRefusal::Full`); a replica's metadata
> (`Green::metadata_bytes`) against `replica_budget` = min(the owner's per-green budget, its shard's room)
> (`OverBudget`, at its making, at a rebuild and after a message); the bytes an owner keeps for them against
> `held_limit` = the per-green budget less the owner's own retention, past which its slowest replica is evicted
> (`FeedRefusal::Evicted`, keeping its frees until it leaves); a change made while the last was unsent evicting every
> replica (one message's blocks recorded at most). **Built (step 5a, 2026-11-18, g083, A-457):** the shards hold a
> green's replicas (`crates/server/src/green_replicas.rs`): the owner makes one on every other shard of the node, up to
> the limit, before the green's first change; feeds each change over the cross-shard carrier; a replica is charged to
> its own shard's budget within its derived budget and leaves, counted, when it refuses a message or its growth; a
> destroyed, fenced, rolled-back or re-installed green's engine retires until every replica left, and the daemon's stop
> closes every shard's replicas and waits for their registrations (no owner dropped with a reader); the limit and
> budgets in the boot profile. **Built (step 5b, 2026-11-18, g083, A-465):** a work's base reads (its files, a page,
> every file's length, at its base version) and its rebase answered by its shard's replica with no hop, by the owner's
> own functions over the replica's engine (byte for byte the owner's, compared whole in the oracle test); what the
> replica cannot serve asked of the owner, counted by why (`merge.replica.route_absent`, `_behind`, `_refused`,
> `_evicted`, `_over_budget`); `merge.replica.served` the non-vacuity counter; a replica that left after a refusal or an
> eviction made again before the owner's next change (`merge.replica.remade`), never one that left for its budget.
> **Built (idle give-back, 2026-11-18, g083, A-473):** a replica no work on its shard has used for its idle window (the
> longest gap it has known between two uses, the first from its holding) is given back, its charge credited
> (`merge.replica.idle_given_back`); only a recorded use arms the shard's one idle check, never a sweep; the first
> request after asks the owner, once, to make it again (`merge.replica.route_idle`), and its next change does
> (`merge.replica.remade`). A replica never used on its shard is not judged idle (no use to derive a window from).
> **A/B (r406, Mac Studio, 2026-11-18): not green.** At 1,000 clients and a 20 ms think, accepted submits' p99 went
> from 0.81, 3.88 and 13.61 ms (three rounds) without the replicas to 60.78, 88.90 and 77.99 ms with them, conflicting
> submits and head reads worse alike: the owner sent every replica each message of the feed inside the submit, before
> its reply, and took an acknowledgement for each. **Built (A-502, 2026-11-18, g083):** the owner queues the feed's
> messages and one task a turn sends each replica's shard the turn's in one message, after every reply of the turn
> (`merge.replica.feed_sent`); each replica acknowledges a turn once (`merge.replica.acknowledged`); a flush whose task
> the arena refuses goes at once, counted (`merge.replica.flush_unarmed`). **A/B again (r100, Mac Studio, 2026-11-19):
> not green.** Head reads and submits at 26.3 to 56.9 ms p50 with the replicas against 0.09 to 1.27 ms without, and every
> kind worse at p99 (110 to 302 ms against 0.23 to 32.9 ms); only an edit's p50 was lower in every round (0.10 to 0.15
> against 0.12 to 0.38 ms), and a rebase's at a 20 ms think (0.22 to 0.45 against 0.29 to 1.36 ms). **Removed (A-528,
> 2026-11-19, g083):** `crates/server/src/green_replicas.rs`, `crates/merge/src/replica.rs`
> and `store.rs`, `crates/merge/tests/replica.rs` and `crates/mem/src/sealed.rs` deleted; the engine's content and
> chunks back in their own memory as before step 1; every call site back to the owner's path. A hypothesis for the
> 26-57 ms p50, not measured, is in the BENCHMARKS record (eviction and remake churn).
>
> **A Shards guest's unprivileged run could not write a host-owned volume: built, the stream takes Shards' owner word
> (2026-11-18, §4.6 the Shards form; A-281; goal g268).** Shards' init names the run's owner on a share's root with
> `trusted.shards.owner` (`UID:GID`), and slates refused it `EOPNOTSUPP`, so a guest of user 1000 saw a Mac's files as
> 501:20 and its kernel refused the run's writes. The stream now takes the word from the guest's root on its root alone
> and refuses it otherwise as Shards' server does. From then on it shows the owner the volume keeps for its root as the
> run's and the run's as the root's, and keeps the ids the guest names the other way round. Every other route sees the
> host's ids, what the run made included. Tests by use: the word's reading and refusals and the dispatch's view
> (`crates/bridge-fuse/tests/shards_fs.rs`), and a real daemon's stream against its NFS port
> (`crates/server/tests/shards.rs`). **Built since (A-290, 2026-11-18):** a guest's `trusted.` and `security.`
> attributes (`security.capability` from `setcap`, `trusted.overlay.*` on an overlayfs upper directory on a share) are
> its data on a Shards stream and slates' own virtio-fs device, never listed or set by a host's FUSE or NFS mount or the
> AppleDouble view, and refused `Unsupported` on a work's declaration; with it, an acknowledged SETXATTR or
> REMOVEXATTR on every FUSE route is published before its reply (it was not: a daemon's death lost it).
> **Built since (A-302, 2026-11-18):** a guest's POSIX ACLs (`setfacl`'s `system.posix_acl_access` and a directory's
> `system.posix_acl_default`) are its data on the same routes, checked as Linux checks one, their named users and
> groups kept through the stream's owner view; stored and not enforced, as Shards' own server keeps them.
> **Built since (A-314, 2026-11-18):** enforced, at Shards' coordinator's ask. A guest route's INIT asks the guest's
> kernel for `FUSE_POSIX_ACL`, so it judges every access by the access ACL it reads; the shared seam keeps Linux's
> rules on every route: the mode is the access ACL's owner, mask and other entries (a set changes the mode, a chmod
> anywhere is read back as the ACL's change, an ACL that says no more than a mode is kept as none), and a directory's
> default ACL is what everything made in it takes, whoever makes it, in place of the umask. Proven by use with a model
> of Linux's permission check over the dispatch's answers (`crates/bridge-fuse/tests/shards_fs.rs`). Not kept: Linux's
> clearing of set-group-ID when a caller outside the file's group sets an ACL, which the FUSE wire carries only under
> `FUSE_SETXATTR_EXT`, not negotiated (a per-connection request form a restored or resynced stream would have to
> carry). (Kept since A-378, below.) Owed: a real guest's run of it (a Shards guest over a stream; a VM over slates' own
> virtio-fs device) and the GETXATTR round trips it adds to a non-owner's access, measured by the integrator.
> **Built since (A-378, 2026-11-18):** an access ACL set from outside a file's group clears the file's set-group-ID
> bit, as Linux does. A guest route's INIT asks for `FUSE_SETXATTR_EXT` beside `FUSE_POSIX_ACL`; each transport reads
> the form from the INIT reply the shared dispatch wrote and tells its bridge (the virtio-fs device before every chain,
> since one pass can serve an INIT and a request after it; a Shards stream before every request); the dispatch then
> reads the extended `fuse_setxattr_in`, and for `system.posix_acl_access` with `FUSE_SETXATTR_ACL_KILL_SGID` clears
> the bit once the ACL is set (a default ACL's set leaves it, as on Linux). A Shards stream keeps the form in its
> anchor-held session (40 bytes; the anchor's cap is 64) and in its SAVE tables (format 2), so a resynced or a restored
> stream, which sees no INIT, reads its guest's requests as before. Found and fixed with it: a RESTORE never told the
> anchor the restored guest's session, so a daemon's death after a restore served the guest with the fresh stream's
> identity owners, the saved swap (A-281) lost. Tables saved before A-378 (format 1) are refused at a RESTORE with
> their reason, as any other format is. Proven by use (a Mac Studio, kiln runs r3591, r3599 and r3623; Linux, GitHub
> run 44357398816): a 02660 file whose access ACL a guest sets with the flag is 0660, one set without it stays 02660, and
> a directory's default ACL leaves its bit; the virtio-fs device serves an extended SETXATTR in the pass that served its
> INIT; a stream reads the form after a restore and after its daemon's death; each of fourteen guards removed alone
> fails its test. Owed: a real guest's run (a non-member's `setfacl` on a set-group-ID file, over a Shards stream and
> over slates' own virtio-fs device).
> **Fixed since (A-587, 2026-11-19):** A-378 left the owner word behind. A Shards stream takes the word before its
> bridge sees the request, and read it in the short form, so after a guest's INIT kept the extended one the word's
> name was read from the setter's flags and the pad, never matched, and the run was shown its share as the host's:
> kiln's macOS microVM drive (r134, kiln 815a790c, slates' A-378 vendored since kiln 688cb98ce) had its stand-in's
> create in its served project refused `EACCES`. The word is read in the form the stream's INIT kept. Tests: the word
> in each form (`crates/bridge-fuse/src/shards_fs.rs`), and a daemon's stream taking it after an INIT that kept the
> extended form, its root then shown as the run's (`crates/server/src/shards.rs`). Swept: no other intercept of the
> stream reads a negotiated form. Owed: kiln's re-vendor and its macOS microVM drive (main's run).
> **Fixed since (A-741, 2026-11-20, w-k90-vendor):** a connection that kept the extended form still sends a SETXATTR
> its kernel sized before INIT's reply arrived in the short form (Linux `fuse_setxattr` sizes by `fc->setxattr_ext`
> at the call; `fuse_block_alloc` holds it until the reply), and Shards' init sets the owner word just then: read in the
> extended form alone, the word fell to the dispatch (`EOPNOTSUPP`) and kiln's macOS microVM g266 drive was refused
> every write `EACCES`, intermittently (recorded on the Mac Studio: `SetXattr` node 1 from uid 0, `setxattr_ext=true`,
> an 8-byte `fuse_setxattr_in`). The form is the request's own now (`abi::setxattr_head`), for the word and the
> dispatch alike. Owed: kiln's re-vendor (with its drive's run).
> **Built since (A-303, 2026-11-18):** a stream's tables for a VM's save and restore (Shards' D176 part 5): a SAVE
> waits for the guest's stores through its maps, takes and publishes a snapshot at the cut and answers tables naming
> it with the guest's references, opens, scope and owner view; a RESTORE, a fresh stream's first frame, takes them onto
> the volume saved while unchanged since the cut or a clone of the cut's snapshot, else `[1, why]` with nothing changed.
> Found with it: a clone keeps no orphan record for a nameless file it carries from its snapshot, so nothing reclaims
> it until the clone is destroyed (any clone of a snapshot taken while a file was held with no name). A SAVE's snapshot
> was published on the owner shard and not waited for at a live-shipped volume's candidates (§4.10). **Built since
> (A-516, 2026-11-19):** a SAVE of a live-shipped volume answers its tables only once the volume's log is durable where
> the save's publication put it, as a guest's `FSYNC` on the stream waits (A-200), and is refused with its reason when
> it is not within the liveness budget (`shards.save_held`, `shards.save_refused`); a volume shipped nowhere is
> answered at once. Proven by the server's lib test over a real stream; Shards' own run of a save and a restore over a
> live-shipped share is owed with its `shards restore` below. **Built since (A-532, 2026-11-19):** the clone's orphan
> record above: a snapshot keeps the orphans it froze (its image too, image version 32), and a clone of it carries each
> with an orphan record, so the clone reclaims the file at its restored guest's let-go, or at a restart's settle when
> nothing holds it, and a clone made after a restart carries them again. Proven by the vfs lib tests (the let-go, and a
> restart rebuilt beside the origin); the server's restore over a clone and a real daemon's restart of one are filed
> for main. A clone made for a restore not yet come keeps its carried files only until a restart.
> **Candidate (A-584's triage, 2026-11-19; recorded, not built, by main's decision):** a RESTORE onto a volume changed
> since the cut, or of a guest that held a file with no name, needs a clone of the cut's snapshot, and nothing outside
> the tables, which are opaque to Shards, tells the caller which snapshot that is: the refusal (`RESTORE_ELSEWHERE`)
> names neither the volume nor the snapshot. A save and then a restore onto the volume unchanged since the cut needs
> nothing more, so Shards' `shards restore` taking a served share and its real-VM test of one need nothing new of
> slates.
> **Still owed for Shards, in its coordinator's order (2026-11-18):**
> - A stream that survives a daemon restart, answering Shards' RESEND, each non-idempotent request (CREATE with
>   O_EXCL, MKDIR, LINK, RENAME, UNLINK) answered at most once from the dead daemon's durable record of its outcome;
>   else the stream ends typed and counted. **Built since (A-316, 2026-11-18), the attach's half, on Linux:** the
>   resync channel beside the stream, its token told to the device first (`Attached`) and kept with the daemon's end,
>   which the anchor holds with the owner view as its session (so the owner view needs no record of its own), handed
>   to the client after the stream (`slates shards --resync-fd`, `ShardsStream::resync`, `CONTRACT` 12). **And the
>   successor's half, on Linux:** recovery keeps a stream whose resync end the anchor held and serves it on a fresh
>   stream, sending the device a `Resync` with its end; a resent request the dead daemon published is answered from its
>   published reply, never run twice; a stream's writes are logged as a mount's are (A-63), which also fixes their loss
>   at a death for streams that are not resynced. **And on macOS (A-339, 2026-11-18), the attach's half:** the channel
>   a stream of 28-byte messages there (a datagram pair's survivor is never told its peer has gone), its device end
>   beside the stream's in the socket route's confirmation, and the daemon keeping its own copy of its held end, since
>   macOS flushes a socket whose every copy rides a message. **And the successor's half on macOS (A-339, the same
>   day):** the write log and its replay, the kept barrier replies, recovery keeping a stream whose end the anchor held,
>   and the successor keeping its copy of the fresh end until the device's first bytes on it or the channel's close.
>   **And its DAX maps (A-365, the same day):** the anchor holds each DAX object a stream hands its device, the shard's
>   DAX range table records each range answered, and a successor takes the objects back, ingests the guest's unsynced
>   stores before it serves anything and answers the device with the same objects; a stream keeps its resync through
>   its guest's maps. **Owed:** Windows on Shards' handle path; its wire is built (A-418, 2026-11-18): a Windows
>   `Resync` names the fresh end's handle in the stream's holder's process, where a successor duplicates it (A-175's
>   route), since no descriptor rides a message there; and the Windows anchor's hold formats for it (A-423, the same
>   day): a resync end is a kind of held entry of one handle, and a daemon replaces a held entry's record as the
>   stream's session moves; and the attach's half (A-427, the same day): the message-mode resync pipe made at the
>   attach, held by the anchor before the stream serves anything, its session and holder told before any reply that
>   rests on them, its device end handed to the client beside the stream's; and the successor's half (A-433, the same
>   day): the held end adopted, a fresh pipe duplicated into the holder the session names (checked by its creation
>   time) and named in a `Resync`, the replies kept for a resend, and `slates shards` handing the end where
>   `{resync}` stands; and its DAX sections (A-448, the same day): the anchor holds a duplicate of each section a
>   resynced stream's guest maps (read, write and query, under the section's confining descriptor) before the answer
>   naming it goes out, its id marked apart from every attachment's, the sections held to a bound of their own
>   (`shards × dax_range_slots`, refused `Bound`); a successor adopts them whole, claims them for the stream and answers
>   the device's asks after the `Resync` with the same sections. Owed on Windows: its real-process restart with DAX on
>   CI's runners (filed for main, `run-requests.md`). **The handoff's length, built since (A-460, the same day):** every
>   held entry rode one environment variable (`SLATES_ANCHOR_HANDLES`), and "the maximum size of a user-defined
>   environment variable is 32,767 characters" (Microsoft Learn, `SetEnvironmentVariableW`'s `lpValue` and "Environment
>   Variables", read 2026-11-18), which a table reaches at about 30 mounts with full records (an entry up to
>   `ENTRY_TEXT_CAP`, about 1,100 characters for a mount, about 90 for a DAX section), while the anchor's bounds admit
>   `shards × 4096` mounts. The table now rides an inherited read-only section of its own length, and the variable names
>   only that section and the length (at most 33 characters); its real-process restart past the limit is filed for

>   Linux and macOS (`SLATES_ANCHOR_DEVICES`, up to 157 characters a device with a session at its 64-byte cap;

>   string passes `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`, `PAGE_SIZE * 32` ("the limit per string is 32 pages": `execve(2)`;
>   `include/uapi/linux/binfmts.h`; 131,072 bytes on 4 KiB pages, about 800 devices with full sessions), failing
>   `E2BIG`, and macOS bounds the arguments and the environment together at `ARG_MAX`, 1,048,576 bytes (`getconf

>   devices: a large holding would leave the anchor unable to start its next daemon. The three parts now ride one sealed,
>   read-only object of their own length (a memfd sealed as a DAX peer's copy is on Linux; an unlinked shared-memory
>   object handed read alone on macOS), and `SLATES_ANCHOR_HELD` names only its descriptor and the length (at most 27

>   `fleet.materialize.given_up` 1) before it released its frozen copy (the give-up logged first, then the release),
>   so the release race named here before was not the cause. A seal leaves a head held by its owner and `f` others,
>   the owner counting its own live copy; at `f = 1` the moved head named a and b alone, and after the switch a's
>   frozen copy answers no fetch, so b's death left no copy any successor could fetch (a successor c would have failed
>   the same way while a let its copy go at c's confirmation). Now a move reports only a head held by `f + 1` members
>   other than the old owner, placing it again on the cohort without the owner at the next sequence and republishing
>   it there when short (A-291's handoff, `Heal::Handoff`, counted `fleet.move.handoff_begun`, which the test now
>   requires); the healer passes a frozen copy by (it had republished the frozen copy's head after b died,
>   `fleet.heal.named_gone` 1, `fleet.heal.republished` 1); and a takeover lets a frozen copy go before it adopts the
>   volume's keys, which the release erases. The test forces the shape it guards: c refuses every content put while a
>   seals the head (so a and b alone hold it), and a and c leave b's move questions unanswered, so b never adopts
>   (`inject_takeover_silence` covers a move's questions by name). Doing so found the operator's own move verb
>   forwarded from the old owner to the target, which never answered it: the move's verb on a frozen copy is now
>   answered there, `Moved` once its routing follows the switch. Red-checked in one tree on the Mac Studio (r3358,
>   0b4ae1111): with the handoff turned off the test fails as it did (`fleet.fetch.no_holder_session` 100,
>   `fleet.materialize.given_up` 1, every read `NotRecovered`), with it on it passes before and after (7.85 s, 5.87 s).
>   An earlier red-check in a second worktree had passed 7 of 7 only because its build shared the green tree's target
>   directory and ran the green binary; a red-check mutates the tree the green run built.
> - **Broken again by A-398's install walk, fixed (2026-11-18, A-485, goal 85 bug 1).** From A-398 on the target-dies
>   test failed every run (4 of 4 on macOS and Linux, main's r242, r277, r327): neither survivor adopted or materialized
>   the moved volume (no `fleet.takeover.adopted`, `fleet.move.adopted` or `fleet.materialize.*` on c), a released its
>   frozen copy, and every read met `NotFound` (Linux) or `HomedElsewhere { region 0 }` (macOS). A-398's per-copy install
>   step followed a move only for a copy routed to a retired host, so at the switch no holder's copy followed: each kept
>   its live old owner's route and authority, no takeover of the dead target listed it, and the configuration handed the
>   volume's line to a successor that never adopted it. Now every copy the walk reaches follows its object's move
>   (`moves::follow_moved_object`); held by `a_held_copy_follows_its_move_at_the_install_walk_and_falls_to_the_dead_
>   targets_successor` (the server's unit tests, red without the fix). Bug record:
>   `docs/bugs/2026-11-18-a-held-copy-of-a-moved-volume-stopped-following-its-move-at-the-install-walk.md`. **Owed

>   2,663 of its content puts, the owner's handoff of the head off itself never finished (`fleet.heal.unfinished` 222),

>   `a_holders_copy_of_a_moved_object_follows_the_move_as_the_install_walk_reaches_it` (`fleet`'s unit tests: the move
>   installed through the walk as the coordinator drives it, then the new owner's next record accepted and the creator's

> - **Owed (the handoff's bound):** the frozen phase lasts as long as the handoff's copy takes, and an unreported move
>   is held to the failover SLO (10 s by default), so a volume whose content cannot be copied to one more host within it
>   is refused `MoveRefusal::Unplaced` and thaws. The fix is to place the head off the owner before freezing (the volume
>   still writable, its later changes then a small incremental seal); not measured yet.
> - **Built (stage 1, A-424, 2026-11-18): a captured clone lands against its capture, judged by content.** Before, a
>   clone of a captured base landed as a scratch volume does: its record names no base and its files hold no witness,
>   so every entry was a create, a file its agent changed met the target's copy as `CreateCreate` (so did an
>   outsider's change to a file the agent never touched), no removal was carried, and a landing that succeeded took the
>   target as the clone's base, after which it no longer moved. Now the landing's manifest is the change of the source
>   since the captured snapshot (`slates_vfs::captured::ChangedPaths`: the inode tables' changed records, each changed
>   directory's entries by name, a made, removed or moved subtree walked whole, a changed file named through its home;
>   skipping the directory nodes the two share is not enough alone, as this entry's plan first said, since a file
>   written in place keeps its directory's node), each entry judged by content against the captured bytes' identity
>   (`content_verdict`): written or removed only over the captured bytes, accepted where the target already holds the
>   volume's, a removed directory removed only once emptied and only when it held nothing else; the write is bound to
>   the object its validation found. An outsider's change to a file the agent never touched is in no manifest. The clone
>   stays a scratch volume (it still moves). Held by the vfs oracle (a whole-tree walk of both trees) and three landings
>   over the simulated host (`crates/land/src/captured_tests.rs`). **Owed, in order:** (1) the advance: a second
>   landing is judged against the capture again, so an outsider's later edit of a file the agent landed and did not
>   touch since is a `ModifyModify` conflict (a refusal, never a loss) until the clone keeps what it landed as its base
>   (a mark snapshot plus the per-path bases of what a filter left out); (2) stage 2 is built (A-503): a move carries
>   the captured state of every path its clone changed in the volume's catalog, and the new owner keeps the moved head as
>   its mark, so a moved clone lands against its capture; and since A-544 every head a captured clone places carries its
>   record, so a takeover after its owner's loss lands it against its capture too (refused by kind where the adopted
>   head has no record, and a move waits for its head's record); since A-565 a live-shipped one's move marks its
>   rebuild from the log too; the fleet's own three-daemon tests of a takeover and of a live-shipped clone's move are
>   written (A-583: `a_captured_clone_taken_over_after_its_owners_loss_lands_against_its_capture` and
>   `a_moved_live_shipped_captured_clone_lands_on_its_new_owner_against_its_capture`, `crates/server/tests/fleet.rs`),
>   and A-503's own move test (A-589:
>   `a_captured_clone_moved_twice_is_whole_on_each_new_owner_and_never_stale_on_an_old_one`, a to b, then b to c),
>   all three compiled and passed unchanged on macOS arm64 (2026-11-19), the Linux lane owed; owed
>   of it, a mark for a live-shipped clone a takeover rebuilt from its log after its owner's loss (the log position its head
>   was sealed at), and a clone whose owner dies before its first snapshot is placed, which its successor serves as an
>   empty tree (sealed at its making, or its catalog naming its capture, A-544; a live one is answered only once its log
>   holds it since A-577);
>   (3) a kind
>   change (a file made a directory) lands as a removal and a making the class order meets as `TypeChanged`; a symlink
>   pointed elsewhere does not land over the old one, as an overlay's does not; (4) the server's own test landing a
>   captured clone into a real directory (run request filed). Kiln's W6 may land captured clones once (1) is built, or
>   now where each workspace lands once.
> - **Decided (the supervisor, 2026-11-18, A-291):** a kiln workspace moves as a clone of a captured base. An overlay
>   keeps its typed refusal (`NotPlain`: its base stays on its source host, §4.10); kiln captures the repository's base
>   once into a complete immutable snapshot (`capture_base`; a git commit's tree checked out where nothing else writes is
>   a quiesced source) and gives each agent an O(1) clone, which moves like a plain volume and survives its runner's
>   loss, the design's preferred delta-plus-base form. Kiln's W3 changes shape (g263, g264 told).
> - **Decided (Ada, 2026-11-18):** the persistent disks Hex gives microVMs stay on their own machine (Hex's D281,
>   "volumes stay per machine", stands); only slates workspaces replicate across kiln runners, so the moves and copies
>   this entry owes are of slates volumes alone.

> **The Node SDK suites on Windows (2026-11-18, §4.7 status "the Node SDK suites end on Windows"; goal 88).** The three
> Node suites had never run on Windows: CI's `sdk` job ran on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` alone. Main's diag run
> 44384411115 (main da697d886) ran them on both Windows runners, and the step went past 70 minutes until cancelled, with
> no log kept. The cause, read from the code: every teardown sent `process.kill(-anchor.pid, 'SIGKILL')`, which Windows
> refuses (libuv opens the process by its id, and there are no groups), and swallowed the refusal; the anchor lived on,
> and its process handle kept `node --test` waiting. **Built:** one teardown the three suites share
> (`crates/sdk-node/tests/anchor.mjs`): the group kill on Unix, and on Windows the anchor's own process ended, whose
> kill-on-close job ends its daemon (`crates/anchor/src/supervise.rs`); a teardown fails its test when the anchor still
> runs 20 s after its kill. CI's `sdk` job gains `windows-latest` and `windows-11-arm` legs that run the Node suites
> and the packaged smoke test, each Node step bounded at 30 minutes; the packaged test's helper is copied beside it in
> `ci.yml`, `.kiln/ci.yaml` and `.kiln/nightly.yaml`. **Owed:**
> - the first Windows run of the three suites (filed for main; red would be a suite failing, not hanging);
> - the Python suites on Windows: the `sdk` job's Python steps assume a Unix venv (`venv/bin/pip`), and the suites
>   themselves start the anchor with `start_new_session` and end it with `os.killpg(os.getpgid(..), SIGKILL)`
>   (`test_sdk.py`, `test_sdk_async.py`), neither of which Windows has, and the async suite's freeze uses `pgrep` and
>   `SIGSTOP` as the Node one does: the same teardown, the anchor's own process ended, is owed there;
> - `every async call ends across restart, silence, reader loss and death` (`sdk_async.test.mjs`) skips loudly on
>   Windows. It freezes the daemon with `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT`, finds the instance's daemons with `pgrep -f` and reads
>   whether each has stopped with `ps -o state=`; none exists there. Its Windows twin freezes each process whole with
>   `NtSuspendProcess`/`NtResumeProcess`, as `crates/cli/tests/start_judgment.rs` does, and finds them by command
>   line; a Node test can make the call only through native code (a test helper the suite spawns, never the shipped
>   addon).

> **git, Mercurial and Subversion over the WinFsp drive (2026-11-17, Part 6 "Real workloads", §4.6; A-300; Ada's
> goal of 2026-11-18).** The Windows lanes (`windows-lint`, `windows-arm64`) now run the roster's four version-control
> workloads (`git`, `git-history`, `mercurial`, `subversion`) over the drive: each script run by Git for Windows' `sh`
> in an NTFS folder of the scratch and on the drive, judged by exit code, output and tree as every leg is. The lanes
> install Mercurial (7.2.4, PyPI's wheel) and Subversion (1.15.0, VisualSVN's command-line zip, SHA-256 pinned). What
> Windows needed: the directory as the root token in each spelling its tools print (`D:\a`, `D:/a`, the shell's
> `/d/a`, a lowercase drive, a canonical path's `\\?\D:\a`); Subversion's file URL in the drive form (`pwd -W`) and
> `svnlook`'s carriage return dropped; and `ln -s` making a real link (`MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict`), so the git
> workload's link goes through the drive's reparse points (A-275), not a copy (on that `ln` alone since A-327, below). **The drive's stated difference:**
> WinFsp's driver makes no hard link (v2.1 answers `FileLinkInformation` `STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` itself,
> `src/sys/fileinfo.c`; its NTFS compatibility page lists hard links unsupported), so a local git or Mercurial clone
> copies on the drive where NTFS links. The three lines that count a clone's files with two names are recorded with
> both sides (`WorkloadStatus::Stated`); every other byte is compared, and a stated line that stops differing fails, so
> the list only shrinks. **Decision for Ada:** hard-linked clones and stores on the WinFsp route need WinFsp's driver
> to pass hard links to its file system, an upstream change to a signed kernel driver (outward-facing); recommended:
> keep the stated difference and offer the change upstream. **2026-11-18, A-360 (goal g258):** the driver change is
> written, two commits on WinFsp v2.1 that apply to v2.2 (`docs/wip/winfsp-patches`, never sent to WinFsp), and the
> drive declares `HardLinks` and serves a forwarded link (its focused tests on both Windows runners). Proven end to end
> on a test-signing Windows Server 2025 VM under KVM (adacachy) with the patched driver: the live `CreateHardLinkW`
> test passes (one file index, two links, the other name reads a write 0.9 ms after the writer's close) and `git clone
> --local` on the drive links all 7 object files, as NTFS does; with WinFsp's own driver the clone dies `failed to
> create link` and the test skips loudly. The decision now comes with the patch in hand: WinFsp's contributor agreement
> (upstream; it assigns joint copyright to WinFsp's author) or an EV code-signing certificate and a Microsoft Partner
> Center account (a slates-signed driver). **A-498 (2026-11-18, g258):** the harness stated the three lines on any WinFsp
> drive, so it failed exactly a patched drive, whose clones link as NTFS's do. It now asks the drive: one file of the
> mount's workload root is given a second name before the workloads run, and the lines are stated only where that is
> refused (`HardLinks`, `mount_links`). On the patched driver git's history and Mercurial are held to every count NTFS
> prints; on WinFsp as released the record notes the refusal and states the lines as before. Owed (main's): that run on
> the test-signing VM, where Mercurial's hard-linked clone and store must come out identical. **The lanes' first run (CI 44260193629, 2026-11-18, x86_64
> and arm64 alike; A-327):** Mercurial identical but for the three stated lines. git and git's history failed on the
> drive alone (`fatal: cannot mkdir .: File exists`, `cannot chdir to upstream.git: No such device`): the shared
> environment's `MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict` also turns Git for Windows' own symbolic links on
> (`compat/mingw.c` `mingw_platform_has_symlinks`), and with them on git resolves every change of directory through
> `GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(VOLUME_NAME_DOS)` (`mingw_chdir`), which Windows answers `ERROR_UNRECOGNIZED_VOLUME`
> (1005) for a drive `DefineDosDeviceW` made; only a drive the Mount Manager made has a final path, and the Mount
> Manager takes Administrators alone (WinFsp issues 410 and 427, its maintainer: no workaround inside WinFsp).
> Subversion failed on both sides: Git for Windows' shell rewrote the argument `^/trunk` as a path,
> `^C:\Program Files\Git\trunk` (svn `E020024`). Fixed: the variable is set on the git workload's `ln -s` alone, so git
> runs as Git for Windows ships it, its symbolic links off; and `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` hands every argument on as
> written. **Corrected the same day (CI run 44271637767, both architectures; A-327):** Subversion ran identical, and
> every `hg` exited 2 on both sides, Python handed `/c/hostedtoolcache/…/Scripts/hg` unconverted (pip's `hg` is a `#!`
> script naming `python.exe`, started with the script's path as its argument) and reading it on drive `D:`. The shared
> environment now leaves only Subversion's `^/` URLs unconverted (`MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=^/`), red-tested by
> `under_the_environment_git_for_windows_sh_starts_hg_and_hands_on_a_relative_url` on both Windows lanes. In the same run
> git and git's history failed on the drive alone, `fatal: detected dubious ownership`, git naming the owner Everyone
> (`S-1-1-0`): the drive answered no security query (WinFsp's DLL refused each, and Windows reported its world
> descriptor), and the one descriptor it held named the Administrators group. **Fixed by A-350:** that descriptor names
> the account the daemon runs as, which every client of a Windows daemon is, for owner and its primary group for group,
> and the drive answers security queries with it, as NTFS reports a file its account made
> (`what_this_account_makes_on_the_drive_reports_it_as_owner_as_ntfs_does`); three winfstest cases that ask for exactly
> its access list pass and are struck (382 to 379). **Then A-368 (the same day):** that access list granted Everyone,
> and any account of any session could open the volume through its kernel name (`\\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\Volume{…}`)
> with the mounting account's rights; it now grants the account, SYSTEM and the Administrators alone, and the mount's
> purge marker (`another_account_cannot_open_a_file_on_the_drive`), and the three cases are listed again (382).
> **Resolved 2026-11-18 by A-369, so no longer for Ada:** the drive is a Mount Manager drive WinFsp's driver makes for
> the unprivileged daemon once the machine allows it (`MountUseMountmgrFromFSD`, set once by an Administrator), and
> Windows resolves every file's final path on it, so git with its symbolic links on works there (WinFsp's memfs as a
> standard account, diagnostics run 44344103821; option (b') below). What A-327 stated: on the drive, git with its
> symbolic links on (Git for Windows'
> installer option, or `core.symlinks=true`) cannot change directory, and so cannot run there; any other program that
> asks a file's final path with `VOLUME_NAME_DOS` is refused the same way (Python's `os.path.realpath` raised it on a
> WinFsp drive in WinFsp issue 427). **Decision for Ada:** (a) state it, the route's limitation (recommended now: no
> privilege is ever required, R10); (b) mount through the Mount Manager (`\\.\X:`), which works and needs an
> Administrator, so only as a choice the person makes when elevated; (b') the same with WinFsp's machine-wide setting
> `MountUseMountmgrFromFSD=1`, which an Administrator sets once (as WinFsp itself is installed once) and which then lets
> an unprivileged mount use the Mount Manager from WinFsp's kernel driver, its drives global to the machine (WinFsp's
> registry-settings page: "not recommended for general use"); (c) mount as a WinFsp network file system, whose
> final path is a UNC path (`\\?\UNC\…`), which every tool would then print in place of the drive. **Shown
> (2026-11-18, diagnostics run 44336880588, with A-327's correction and A-350):** on both Windows runners git and
> Subversion ran identical over the drive, and git's history and Mercurial identical but for the drive's stated
> hard-link lines; the cell's record (`native-windows-winfsp.workloads.json`, the owed skip of 2026-11-05 until then) is
> re-recorded from the x86_64 run. **Open:** the roster's other workloads (cargo, npm, python, rg, rsync, sqlite, editor,
> watcher) are owed a Windows form.

> **A delete racing a coherent purge can hang its caller in the WinFsp drive (found 2026-11-18 by A-360's race on the
> test-signing VM; open, Windows; the dropped delete found beside it is fixed, docs/bugs/2026-11-18-a-delete-a-purges-last-handle-carried-was-dropped.md).**
> The race: `a<n>` linked to `b<n>`, `a<n>` held open so the mount's next round purges it (A-190), a write through
> `b<n>`, then `a<n>` closed and deleted at once (`vm-delete-race.ps1`). In 4 of 4 runs, the deleter hung within 60
> rounds: at rounds 28 and 17 before the fix, and at 60 and 1 after it. Its thread waits in `NtClose` (`IopCloseFile`) for its
> cleanup IRP. Local kernel debugging at round 1 (`kd -kl`, 2026-11-18 18:52 UTC, `hang-kd-1`; read again from the
> dump the same day, which corrects two lines first written here) showed:
> - **The receive worker was not idle: it was sending an answer.** Its one IRP had a buffered input and no MDL (flags
>   `0x60830`, `Mdl 0`). In `crate::dispatcher` only `send` makes that IRP (`TRANSACT_BATCH`, the answer as input, no
>   output); a receive's output is an MDL. The thread waited in kernel mode in `FsRtlCancellableWaitForSingleObject`,
>   called from FltMgr (return address `fffff804'1b2821cf`, inside FLTMGR at `fffff804'1b260000`-`1b2f5000` by `lm a`
>   in `hang-kd-4`).
> - **The purge client was not idle on its pipe: it was opening a file.** Its only thread held a Create IRP (flags
>   `0x884`) and waited at the same FltMgr return address. The pipe wait was the mount thread's: a pending read of the
>   client's answer.
> - The deleter, the receive worker, the purge client and the mount thread all began waiting at one tick (5988).
> - One resource was held shared, alone, by a request. In WinFsp's source a request holds a single resource shared only
>   as a Create's rename lock (WinFsp v2.1 `src/sys/create.c:246` and `669`): the purge client's open.
> - One file node's two resources were held shared by another request, with one exclusive waiter (a system worker) and
>   a contention count of 6. WinFsp leaves a node shared to a request only for a non-cached or paging read
>   (`src/sys/read.c:357-444`), an information query (`src/sys/fileinfo.c:1024-1102`), a stream query (`763-790`), a
>   security query (`src/sys/security.c:77-109`), a device control (`src/sys/devctl.c:268`) or a reparse point's
>   read (`src/sys/fsctl.c:339`). Each of these waits for a receive.
> - A second system worker held one resource exclusive and a second one on its own stack.
>
> **The mechanism the source gives (a hypothesis that fits every waiter; not proven).**
> **Shown for fsx's wedge (2026-11-20, goal 87, w-bugs; goal-83 B3):** on CI's windows-latest the receive worker began
> sending a shrink's SetInformation answer and that `DeviceIoControl` never returned (about 59 s, then the run's end);
> every earlier send returned within 481 µs and no request was received after it (diagnostics branch
> `diag-w-bugs-b3-9`; record `docs/bugs/2026-11-05-winfstest-found-win32-semantics-the-drive-broke.md`, "Shown
> 2026-11-20"). SetInformation's completion runs `CcSetFileSizes` on the sender (`fileinfo.c` 1407, `file.c` 1852), so
> the one receiver waits on the drive it alone receives for. **Fixed by A-725 (2026-11-20):** a relief receiver with its own journal
> serves while the primary is held in a send (`crate::inflight::relief`); fsx seed 1 now runs whole over the drive.
> Open: whether the delete racing a coherent purge above had the same cause (the VM race, rerun with A-725); a relief
> held in a send of its own is relieved by no one.
> - WinFsp completes an answered IRP inline, on the thread that sent the answer. `FspVolumeTransact`
>   (`src/sys/volume.c:1089-1102`) calls `FspIopDispatchComplete` for each answer, and the kind's `FSP_LEAVE_IOC`
>   (`src/sys/driver.h:289-306`) ends in `IoCompleteRequest` (`src/sys/iop.c:321`).
> - So the completion routines of every driver above WinFsp run on slates' receive worker. FltMgr's run there, and with
>   them each minifilter's post-operation callback that FltMgr does not hand back to the requester's thread.
> - slates has one receiver (A-198; `crate::dispatcher`'s `Worker`, "the only receive thread"). If a filter's completion
>   makes a synchronous request on the same drive, the worker waits inside FltMgr for a request only it can receive,
>   and the drive stops. Then the purge client's open, the request holding the node, the deleter's cleanup and the
>   system worker that wants the node exclusive all wait on that worker.
> - WinFsp's own dispatcher survives such nesting: it runs at least two receive threads (`src/dll/fs.c:26`, `384-401`;
>   by default one per processor, 4 to 16), so another thread takes the filter's request.
> - The filter is likely Defender's (WdFilter): the VM runs MsMpEng with real-time protection on. On CI's x86_64
>   runner, something the bench never called asked one QuerySecurity per Cleanup (273,006 in g258's diag-52 probe;
>   none on arm64), which is a filter's pattern.
> - Unproven: which IRP the worker's answer completed, and which filter waited. The worker's stack ends at FltMgr's
>   first frame, because FltMgr's symbols were not loaded.
> - **Cured by A-725, shown by use on WinFsp as released (2026-11-20, w-bugs, goal 87):** the race with an outside
>   writer in place of the link (`crates/cli/tests/winfsp.rs`
>   `a_delete_racing_a_coherent_purge_returns_and_removes_the_file`: 60 rounds of an SDK write, a held open through the
>   drive, an SDK rewrite whose round purges it, then the close and delete at once). On main just before A-725, on CI's
>   x86_64 runner, 2 of 3 runs hung: one deleter past 10 s at round 7, one test process stuck at round 43 until the
>   step's 900 s bound (diag-w-bugs-race-old-1); with A-725's relief receiver 6 of 6 runs passed whole on x86_64 and
>   arm64 (diag-w-bugs-race-new-1). The VM race on the patched driver is not rerun (no VM here).
> - **The fix, once confirmed, is slates':** a receive must never wait for a send's completion. One way is a second
>   receiver, WinFsp's own posture; A-198's capture-and-settle order assumes one, so this is a design amendment.
>   Another way is to send from a thread that does not receive.
> - **Impact when unrecovered.** The process cannot exit while the daemon lives, and on the first run the daemon did not
>   exit when its anchor was killed. Windows' restart then hung past 15 minutes, and a reset was needed.
> - **Not known yet:** which request holds the node (the owner pointer's `Kind` and IRP), whether the hang needs a
>   filter (the race with Defender's real-time protection off), and whether WinFsp as released reaches it. There, a purge
>   follows a change from outside a file's open names (A-190) rather than a hard link's.
> - **Also open:** 3 of 59 deletes were refused `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` in that race with the fix in place, where NTFS
>   deletes.
> - **Owed** (filed to main, run-requests 2026-11-18):
>   - `vm-hang-probe2.ps1` on the VM, which dumps the owner request and its IRP when the race stops, now with FltMgr's
>     symbols loaded, the receive worker's whole stack and `fltmc instances`;
>   - the 60-round race three times with Defender's real-time protection off, against three times with it on;
>   - the same race on WinFsp's own driver, with an outside writer in place of the link.

> **The WinFsp drive declared a folding volume case-sensitive (found 2026-11-17 reading WinFsp v2.1's source for A-300;
> built 2026-11-19 in two parts, A-543 and A-551; the Windows half compiled and run by main, owed).** The mount set
> `CaseSensitiveSearch` (and `CasePreservedNames`) for every volume (`crates/bridge-winfsp/src/host.rs`, the mount's
> `params.flags`), while a volume made with `--fold` (`NamePolicy::Fold`) folds names in its own look-ups. WinFsp's
> driver keys its open files by name and compares case-sensitively when that bit is set (`src/sys/device.c` 676 and 750,
> `src/sys/create.c` 316-318). So a file opened as `A.TXT` and as `a.txt` on a folding volume got two of the driver's
> file nodes: two share-access records (an exclusive open does not exclude the other spelling, where NTFS answers a
> sharing violation) and two caches over one file. T-4.6 ("case-insensitive lookup on a case-fold volume; expect one
> entry and `EEXIST` on a folded duplicate") had no test through the drive. The fix: declare `CaseSensitiveSearch` for
> an exact volume only, and answer each open of a folding volume with its normalized name (each component as stored),
> which WinFsp otherwise upper-cases (`create.c` 1036-1043), failing test first (an exclusive open under one spelling,
> then the other: NTFS's `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`). The roster's workloads open no file under two spellings, so the
> Windows workloads cell, which runs on a folding volume to match NTFS (A-300), does not meet it.
> - **Built, part 1 of 2 (2026-11-18, A-543, goal 85, g079): the path an open names as the volume stores it.**
>   `slates_bridge_core::stored_path` walks a `\`-separated path from the root and names each component as its
>   directory stores it (`Bridge::stored_entry`, over `Volume::stored_name_no`): on a folding volume every spelling of a
>   file answers the spelling it was made with, on an exact one the path as asked. Held by
>   `every_spelling_of_a_file_on_a_folding_volume_names_the_path_it_was_made_with` (bridge-core's unit tests, every
>   host), red with the open named as asked on the Mac Studio.
> - **Built, part 2 of 2 (2026-11-19, A-551, goal 85, g258): the drive's half.** The drive declares
>   `CaseSensitiveSearch` for an exact volume only (`Mounted::new`, given the volume's policy by
>   `crates/server/src/winfsp.rs` `name_search`); the held record keeps the posture, so a successor serves a drive as it
>   was mounted, and a record made before A-551 reads as case-sensitive, as every drive then was. Each open and create
>   on a folding drive answers its node's name as WinFsp's normalized name (`FSP_FSCTL_OPEN_FILE_INFO`, `finish_open`):
>   each prefix as Windows already holds it, else the stored spelling where the driver takes it for the asked one (the
>   system's upcase table, ntdll's `RtlUpcaseUnicodeChar`), else as asked (`crates/bridge-winfsp/src/normalized.rs`);
>   the open's ledger record and `OpenNames` keep that name byte for byte, as the driver renames and notifications need
>   it (`winfsp.h` 1285-1299). The receive worker clears what WinFsp's DLL counts past a Create's name and descriptor:
>   v2.1 counts the name twice when it places the descriptor (`fsop.c` 468 then 413), which would have sent the
>   packet's earlier bytes. Pure rules held by unit tests on every host (`normalized::tests`, `notify::tests`'s
>   `the_spelling_windows_holds_a_path_by_follows_opens_closes_and_renames`, `inflight::tests`'s
>   `a_create_answered_with_a_name_and_a_descriptor_sends_no_byte_of_an_earlier_response`, `held::tests`'s
>   `the_mount_record_keeps_how_its_drive_compares_names`).
> - **Run and red-checked (2026-11-20, w-bugs, goal 87; CI windows-latest and windows-11-arm):** A-551's two drive
>   tests pass on both architectures; with `CaseSensitiveSearch` declared for every volume (the rule before A-551)
>   `every_spelling_of_a_file_on_a_folding_drive_is_one_file_to_windows` fails and the exact one still passes
>   (diag-w-bugs-win-green-1 / -red-1). A-576's case, held by use under Windows' own table (A-737):
>   `names_windows_folds_alike_are_one_file_on_a_folding_drive_and_final_sigma_is_two` (`ɐ`/`Ɐ` one file, `ς`/`σ` two,
>   as on NTFS) passes, and fails with the same forced flag. The roster's git, Mercurial and Subversion workloads pass
>   over the drive on both (WinFsp as released makes no hard link, so the stated hard-link lines apply).
>   A-551's other two parts, each red-checked apart on both architectures: the sharing violation (with
>   `CaseSensitiveSearch` forced, `a.txt` opened beside an unshared `A.TXT`: `Ok(())` where `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`
>   was expected; diag-w-bugs-win-red-1), and the stored spelling as WinFsp's normalized name (with no normalized name
>   answered, the sharing violation held but `CAFÉ.TXT`'s final path read `CAFÉ.TXT` where the stored `Café.txt` was
>   expected; diag-w-bugs-win-nred-1), both in `every_spelling_of_a_file_on_a_folding_drive_is_one_file_to_windows`.
> - **Owed (main, filed in run-requests.md):** the Windows build of A-551 (`host.rs`, the server's `winfsp.rs`) and the
>   drive tests `every_spelling_of_a_file_on_a_folding_drive_is_one_file_to_windows` (red before: `a.txt` opened beside
>   an unshared `A.TXT`, final path `a.txt`) and `an_exact_drive_keeps_two_spellings_two_files`
>   (`crates/cli/tests/winfsp_semantics.rs`), with the rest of the WinFsp suites.
> - **Out of reach, stated (A-551):** names the volume folds alike and Windows' upcase table does not (a decomposed `é`
>   against a precomposed one, the Kelvin sign against `K`) stay a file node per spelling, since the driver refuses a
>   normalized name that differs by more than its table's case; a path past 1,024 units is upper-cased by the driver
>   (the DLL drops a longer normalized name), so a rename of a directory above it that the records spell otherwise
>   leaves that record behind; and names the table folds alike and the volume keeps apart (final sigma `ς` against `σ`)
>   are two files to the volume and one node to the driver, so the second's open while the first is open shares the
>   first's node and cache. Decided 2026-11-19 (the coordinator, from principle): the volume refuses the twin at create,
>   so the state is never reachable; a refusal at the second open would leave it.
> - **Built, A-576 part 1 (2026-11-19, goal 85, g258): a volume can fold by Windows' own upcase table.**
>   `NameEquivalence::Upcase` folds each UTF-16 unit through Microsoft's recommended exFAT up-case table (specification
>   Table 25, TableChecksum E619D30Dh, 874 units mapped; `crates/vfs/src/upcase.rs`), unit for unit with no
>   normalization, as WinFsp's driver compares: `ς` beside `σ` is refused `EEXIST` at create and link, a rename onto it
>   replaces the entry, and a decomposed and a precomposed `é` are two names. Such a volume and its drive take the same
>   names for one, so neither residual above that comes from the two rules (the first and the last) can arise on it.
>   Held by vfs's unit tests on every host (red 5 of 10 with the table removed, green 10 of 10, Mac Studio).
> - **Fixed, A-737 (2026-11-20, w-bugs, goal 87; found by use): the table was not Windows'.** The Windows check
>   (`the_volumes_upcase_table_is_the_systems`) failed on CI's x86_64 and arm64 runners: 109 units apart. Windows' own
>   table (dumped through `RtlUpcaseUnicodeChar` on both, identical: 973 units mapped, no two to one, TableChecksum of
>   the whole table E61F453Bh) leaves final sigma `ς` as it is, folds the case pairs Unicode added after the exFAT
>   table (`ɐ`/`Ɐ`, `ͱ`/`Ͱ`, ...), and leaves `Ⱥ` (the exFAT table mapped it to the lowercase `ⱥ`). `Upcase` now folds by
>   Windows' table; the "names the table folds alike and the volume keeps apart" residual above does not arise (every
>   pair it folds alike, NFC and lowercasing fold alike too), and `ς` beside `σ` is two names, as on NTFS. No volume was
>   made `Upcase` before (no client can choose it until part 2), so no stored name changes meaning.
> - **Owed, A-576 part 2:** the policy in the protocol and the catalog (`NamePolicy`, `DbNamePolicy`, appended and
>   published), its choice in the CLI, the SDKs and MCP, an archive importing it (refused `Unsupported` until then), and
>   what a WinFsp mount of a `Fold` volume does once a drive's volume can be made `Upcase`. Main's: the Windows check
>   that the system's table is the volume core's at every unit (`the_volumes_upcase_table_is_the_systems`).
