> **Windows gives freed content pages back (A-205, 2026-11-04), and the audit's held-section leak was not one.** A deleted
> file's pages leave a Windows daemon's working set at the idle purge, and a block reusing them is zeroed before it is
> handed out. The section's commit stays charged, by design: Windows has no decommit for a view of a section. The audit's
> "a refused view leaks the held section's handle" was wrong: `view` closed it, 0 handles in 200 refused adoptions on
> unchanged code and 200 with the close removed (`crates/mem/tests/held_section.rs`); the adoption now maps first anyway.
> Numbers and CI runs: BENCHMARKS, "What a write costs on pages given back on Windows".

> **Fixed 2026-11-05 (A-202, agents/perf):** a submit no longer clones, walks or hashes the whole green; every verdict
> form's median is 51–69 µs at 10 to 10,000 files (BENCHMARKS, "A full edit and merge"). The record below stays as found.
>
> **A merge's cost grows with its green's file count (2026-11-05, RQ-4, §4.16; found open).** The new
> `crates/client/examples/edit_merge_bench.rs` measures, on macOS arm64 at load 9, an accepted submit's median at
> 25–161 µs over a green's first hundred versions and 529–684 µs over its last hundred (six runs). Each version adds a
> file. One file replaced 1,000 times shows no growth, and an edit shows none in either form. Every submit clones
> each path of the green (`Green::current_base`), walks each base file (`compose_volume`), and hashes each byte of the
> green (`Green::head_identity` in `merge_service::enqueue_record`). That puts RQ-4's millisecond out of reach for a
> repository-sized green. The fix is the perf agent's. The clients agent re-measures merge on every platform once it
> lands. Also open from the same runs: a sevenfold p50 split between two invocations on this Mac (edit 18.8 against
> 2.5 µs). Record: `BENCHMARKS.md`, "The client's edit and merge latency".

> **Replication latency (raft, 2026-11-04): a commit returns at its quorum; live shipping in the daemon: writes durable on a candidate before their reply, takeover serves them.** Every quorum
> collector in `slates-cluster` slept its whole poll after its quorum had answered, so a cross-node record commit cost
> the daemon's 10 ms poll (10,125–10,194 µs at the median) over a 12 µs loopback round trip. Each reply now wakes its
> collector: 18.9–19.9 µs at the median, p99 28.8–32.9 µs, worst 44.7 µs at the daemon's poll
> (`replication_bench`, five interleaved rounds at load 36–42, `docs/wip/BENCHMARKS.md`; failing test first:
> `a_commit_returns_at_its_quorum_not_at_its_poll`; record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-11-04-a-quorum-collector-waited-out-its-poll.md`). Live shipping's log (A-200) is built and checked
> as a pure module (`crates/db/src/live.rs`; the nemesis in `crates/db/tests/live.rs`: 200 seeds × 3,000 steps at f=1
> and f=2, Agreement, NoLoss, StaleNeverCommits and Convergence held, each check red under a mutation; §4.10 status).
> Over the fleet transport (`crates/cluster/src/live.rs`) a live-shipped write is durable on two hosts in 17–20 µs at
> the median for 64 B and 23–27 µs for 4 KiB, every quiet p99 under 1 ms (64 KiB: 160–292 µs), unchanged with one
> holder dead (BENCHMARKS "Live shipping over the transport"). Found on the way, and explained 2026-11-08: a
> session's round trip in `crates/cluster/tests/live.rs` grew about 1.7 times an exchange (9, 14, 23 … 621 ms of virtual
> time). That test's sockets were OS sockets, which the simulation driver never watched, so its sessions were woken
> only by their timers (`docs/bugs/2026-11-08-an-os-socket-awaited-on-the-simulation-driver-woke-only-on-its-timers.md`).
> Bound on the fabric, each write takes no virtual time. The policy is built: `slates live-ship ID [--off]` records it on the owner partition,
> `list` shows it, the catalog register carries it, and the db model test recovers it
> (`crates/server/tests/live_ship.rs`). The daemon ships (2026-11-05, §4.10 status "slice one"): across three real
> daemon processes a live volume's writes reach both candidates and become durable (`crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`,
> 4 of 4). Barriers wait (§4.10 status "slice two"): a recorded verb and a stable NFS write or `COMMIT` on a live
> volume are answered only once a candidate holds them, red-checked across real processes. Takeover reads the live
> log (§4.10 status "slice three"): a never-sealed live volume's five acknowledged writes survive its owner's SIGKILL,
> served whole by a survivor in 1.8–2.3 s, empty without the log; a live write also waits for its volume's head
> placement, so an owner killed the moment its last write returns loses nothing (3 of 3; 2 of 2 lost everything
> before). Chaos across real processes (§4.10 status): a candidate partitioned away (SIGSTOP) and healed, and both
> candidates stalled in overlapping 30 ms windows through 30 writes, each write durable at its return (stall p90
> 33 ms, max 47 ms) and every candidate caught up after; the partition found a live exchange budget a stopped peer
> inflated, now the liveness budget with dead links redialed. A superseded owner resumed after its takeover never has a
> write acknowledged; writers killed mid-write leave the log whole and no reply held; a destroyed volume's copies are
> let go (three defects found and fixed on the way: §4.10 status "Chaos, continued"). Open: hard links and extended
> attributes in the rebuilt volume; a candidate's copy across its own daemon's restart. FUSE `fsync` on a live volume is
> answered at durability since 2026-11-05 (`EIO` past the liveness budget; §4.10 status "FUSE `fsync` at durability"). So are a Shards
> stream's `FSYNC` (`EIO` after 1.001–1.003 s with both candidates stopped, where it answered `0` in 337 µs), a writable
> map's `MapSync` and a checkout into a live base (each answered with nothing durable before; now they wait as a verb
> does); NFSv4 shares the v3 wait; a virtio-fs or vhost-user `FSYNC` (`EIO` after 1.0006–1.0017 s, where it
> answered `0` in under 1 ms) and a WinFsp flush (error after 1.001–1.028 s, where it succeeded in 995 µs; a volume
> flush now publishes at all) wait too (§4.10 status "Every other durability claim"). Open (live-durability): one x86_64
> virtio-fs run of 19 answered a stopped `FSYNC` `0` after 1.000358 s, unexplained; that run printed no log line, and
> the 16 runs since, which print the owner's log and the hold's counters at that point, never repeated it. Fixed (g227, 2026-11-18): the position every transport's claim waits for (`live_ship::durable_target`) ignored a
record the volume owed while the fleet did not yet know it (its head unplaced). A publication that could not become an
entry (the credit full with the candidates stopped) owes a whole record at the head's next position, but the unplaced
case returned the head as it stood: with nothing shipped yet the reply waited for nothing, and with a head it waited one
position short, so once the head was placed the claim was answered while the write it named was only in the record
still owed. The decision is now one pure function (`owed_position`), the owed record counted placed or not; its unit
test (`a_reply_whose_publication_owes_a_whole_record_waits_for_that_record_placed_or_not`) was red first. Whether this
was the stopped `FSYNC` answered `0` above is not shown: that run printed no log line. Open
> (live-fixes): a Windows fleet did not re-form after an anchor succeeded a suspended candidate under a fresh identity.
> Measured in the daemon (release, BENCHMARKS "What live shipping adds to a stable NFS write"): a live 4 KiB `FILE_SYNC`
> write costs 90–114 µs more than a plain one at the median, p99 217–398 µs, p999 0.44–1.27 ms, worst 0.47–1.87 ms at
> load 8–30 (2026-11-05). The rare 100 ms tail is explained and removed (two waits for the record period; and a
> superseded owner that held a write unanswered is now refused, and a destroyed volume's shipper is let go: §4.10
> status "The tail and three more defects"). Open: the added median is the cross-shard dispatch round (50 µs not met);
> p999 under 1 ms at load 30. Since 2026-11-18 the round is counted hop by hop on the owner (§4.10 status "The round,
> counted hop by hop": `fleet.live.hop.*`, the hops adding up to the round exactly); its breakdown under the contract
> command is owed. A-396 (2026-11-18): the round's cost was parked threads, not the hop; each shard on a write's path
> asks to hold its idle window across its wait, the windows learned from the traffic, each hold kept only while the
> shard's measured idle turn is shorter than its wake (A-387's predicate: a macOS shard declines). First A/B at load
> 78–93 (adacachy): added 86–115 µs against main's 186–295, but the live p999 not better (4.2–27.7 ms against 2.6–15.1)
> and the plain write's p99 worse (293–1,024 against 132–785 µs): suspected the unit's CPU quota spent by the spinning
> shards; landed before its A/B (Ada's rule of 2026-11-18), the supervisor's A/B with `nr_throttled` is owed and
> decides whether the holds stay. Since 2026-11-07 a live volume's log goes to each holder on its own lane, the holders at once, only
> to holders of its catalog, and a lane waits for its requests before it ends (§4.10 status "One lane a holder"): a
> write no longer waits for a stopped candidate (main: 406–1,064 ms for the first write after a stop, now 3–99 ms), and
> no holder's session is left lent with a cancelled request (KIND `wan`, `wan-loss` and `ceiling` acknowledged every
> write, where main stalled; the lanes alone did too, so KIND does not separate the stragglers' wait; its failing test is on the simulated fabric, `a_lane_that_ends_with_a_holder_unanswered_gets_every_session_back`). Open: a large install over a slow path is still cut at the live budget, as on main; it
> waits on raft-chaos's size-derived exchange budget. And a lane may wait one record period for a session the record
> plane has lent (`ship_head`). Fixed the same day: a holder behind the retained tail no longer puts a whole copy of the volume on the log ahead of every later write; it is installed from an image made beside the log (§4.10 status "An install image beside the log"). Open: one exchange per message to every holder starved the second holder (never
> accepted an entry, in six of nine process flows) and was rejected; why is not pinned down. Open, toward a filesystem
> server replicated per write in under 1 ms: AC-8.9's credit backpressure (since 2026-11-05 a local checkpoint ships a
> live volume's changes, not a whole copy: 1 whole record in 2,051 where main made about 420; since 2026-11-17 the credit
> is the whole state's bytes, not a fixed two entries, A-200 amended, the entry at the top of this ledger); a candidate's copy kept across its own
> restart; real-process chaos
> (partitions, injected latency, volume failure, client disconnect). The volume-failure and client-disconnect faults
> are in the register's simulation since A-585 (g250, 2026-11-19, goal 81): `ledger::Cohort::lose_store` (a store lost
> under a replica: the holder answers no read and accepts no record under its old id, as a fresh-id restart does), with
> `a_holder_whose_store_is_lost_answers_nothing_under_its_old_id` (red before: a store-lost holder answering with nothing
> completed a quorum that missed a committed record at `f = 2`) and `a_write_its_client_left_is_kept_or_dropped_whole`;
> the real-process runs of both faults are main's (run-requests.md): the store-destroyed flows exist, and the client
> killed mid-write is `a_client_killed_mid_write_leaves_its_write_whole_or_absent_through_a_takeover` (`live_chaos.rs`,
> 2026-11-19: its write killed between sent and answered by the owner's `fleet.live.awaited`, the owner then lost, the
> next owner judged by every invariant). The owner's `put_wal` is its `Local` records,
> resumed by the record period after a warm restart (2026-11-17, g230; §4.8 "Recovery" status,
> `a_seal_its_owner_had_not_placed_at_a_warm_restart_places_after_it`); the loss-window report is unbuilt; a head still
> waits up to the 100 ms record period before its commit starts.
> **Fixed 2026-11-05 on agents/raft-2 (bug record `docs/bugs/2026-11-05-a-live-takeover-counted-no-empty-report-and-fenced-no-empty-copy.md`):
> a live takeover could wait for its quorum and never serve, and phase one had a safety hole.** The hypothesis below held.
> A successor that held no copy never counted itself (`fetch`), and a remote candidate that held no copy answered "none"
> without raising a fence (`serve_fetch`). The second is a **safety defect**, on main since 7f57f1b6 (slice three,
> landed in 2f343fcd) for opt-in live-shipped volumes: the db nemesis model, extended so a candidate's copy exists only
> once a message reaches it, fails StaleNeverCommits in 10 of 400 seeds when an empty report counts without a fence. In
> f=1 seed 27: the owner (host 1, epoch 1) had shipped nothing; host 3 took over at epoch 2 on two empty reports (hosts 2
> and 3); host 3 appended position 0 = 1; host 1, resumed, appended its own position 0 = 3, which host 2 (no copy, no
> fence, still taking host 1 for the owner) accepted, so position 0 was durable twice with two values. Fixed by
> `live_ship::fenced_copy` at both sites: a candidate with no copy makes an empty one with its fence at the takeover's
> epoch, and its report counts. Every invariant then holds (f=1: 110 takeovers, 57 empty reports; f=2: 241, 145); the
> mutation stays as a test (`an_empty_report_without_a_fence_lets_a_superseded_owner_commit`). The liveness side is red
> first and green after across real processes (`a_successor_that_holds_no_copy_still_takes_a_live_volume_over`: the
> successor waited 397 times and never served; after, served in 3.2 s). A refused entry never counts as held
> (`a_refused_entry_is_never_counted_as_held`). Still open, found on the way: why a candidate holds no copy. Holders now
> count refusals by reason (`fleet.live.hold_refused.*`). Over three loaded runs one candidate refused the owner
> `not_a_member` 22 times and then held the log (a membership lag at the fleet's start), but another refused 6 times
> `not_a_member` and then 21 times `no_catalog` and held nothing for the whole run: a candidate that never receives the
> volume's catalog keeps refusing, and the log rests on the other candidate alone (with it stopped, writes cannot be
> durable; a soak run hung on exactly that). Owner: raft, next.
>
> **Found 2026-11-06 (raft), fixed 2026-11-07 (A-250): a restarted council leader never condemned a member that died
> during its restart.**
> Under anchors, with a candidate's daemon restarted warm while the owner was stopped and then killed, no takeover
> began in 40 s: the restarted node led the council (term 2, three voters) and still listed the owner a member, but its
> failure detector held no entry for it (the owner was already stopped when it came back, so it never heard from it and
> never suspected it); the other survivor had dropped the owner. The reproduction is
> `a_candidates_restored_copy_serves_its_owners_takeover` (`crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`, ignored until 2026-11-09).
> Root cause (read from the code, 2026-11-07): a node joins a member to its failure detector only once a session keyed
> it (`member_task::join_addressable` reads `plane.keyed`), and its detector ignores gossip about members it has not
> joined (AUD-15: no authenticated peer can name arbitrary targets). A member already down when the node restarts is
> never keyed, so never joined, and the survivors' gossip of its death is dropped. Proposed fix, not yet built: also
> join every member the committed configuration names whose address resolves, keyed or not. The configuration
> authorizes them, so AUD-15's bound holds. The peers' death gossip then reaches the restarted node, while its own
> unsendable probes stay no misses (the KIND rule in `MemberPlane::join`).
> Closed by A-250 (caf06d71; the 2026-11-07 entry "a member down through a voter's restart was never taken over"): a
> death is retired at `f + 1` voters, and a restarted voter watches every configured member, the join proposed above.
> The reproduction runs again since it shares its volume with every node first (b79bae7b, 2026-11-09): `live_fleet` 31
> of 31, three runs in a row (adacachy, 2026-11-11, 2c93f4c9). The holder's live copies rode its recovery image rebuilt
> whole at each acknowledgement (`live_ship::acknowledged`, about 100 µs a live write, growing with what a candidate
> keeps); since A-270 a publication carries only the pieces that changed (the 2026-11-08 entry).
>
> **As found, landing 13 (2026-11-05): a live takeover can wait for its quorum and never serve.** On adacachy in a
> capped unit (`CPUQuota=1200%`, load 18–25), `a_superseded_owner_resumed_after_its_takeover_is_fenced`
> (`crates/cli/tests/live_fleet.rs`) failed 1 of 2 runs on the landing's tree: with the owner stopped, the survivor that
> adopted the takeover (`fleet.takeover.adopted` 2) waited for its live log's quorum for the whole 40 s
> (`fleet.live.takeover_waits_quorum` 370, `fleet.live.hold_refused` 14) and refused every read `Overloaded`, while the
> other candidate answered its fetches (`fleet.live.fetched` 400) and held the log at head 2. No acknowledged write was
> lost (the candidate held all three); the volume went unserved. The same signature on macOS (load 13–21), in
> `a_live_volumes_acknowledged_writes_survive_its_owners_death`, 1 of 9 runs: the successor waited 371 times
> (`fleet.takeover.adopted` 2, `fleet.live.hold_refused` 28) while the other candidate answered 421 fetches holding head
> 4. In both, the successor holds no copy of the log (no `live held` line; it had refused the owner's entries). A
> hypothesis from the counters and the code, not yet confirmed by a log line: `live_ship::fetch` adds the successor's
> own report only when it holds a copy, while a remote candidate that holds nothing answers `None` and counts, so a
> successor holding nothing never counts itself and `f + 1` is out of reach once the owner is gone. Owner: raft,
> before any other live-shipping work.
>
> **Chaos from outside the processes (raft-chaos, 2026-11-06): defects fixed and open, below.**
> The harness is `crates/cli/tests/live_chaos.rs` (`SLATES_TEST_CLI=1`): three fleet daemons, a Rust client streaming
> 4 KiB writes, every node's live lines sampled throughout (status now prints each log's head epoch, chain identity and
> fence), and each flow ending with the register invariants checked from outside the processes:
> - Agreement: one identity at every epoch and position any copy reported;
> - NoLoss: every acknowledged write served byte for byte, nothing torn;
> - StaleNeverCommits: writes through a superseded owner refused, survivors fenced at the takeover's epoch;
> - Convergence: every candidate at the owner's head, durable, nothing owed.
>
> - **Built, first runs owed (g229, 2026-11-17): loss, a running node cut off, and ReadSafety and Continuity across
>   real processes.** SIGSTOP stops a whole process and drops nothing, so until now no flow here injected loss, kept an
>   isolated owner running (its lease lapsing, its peers judged dead from its side), or cut one direction only; only
>   KIND's netem injected loss (`cargo xtask kind live`, which no lane runs).
>   - A node may bind elsewhere than it advertises (A-277, the manifest's `bind`), so the fault relay
>     (`crates/cli/tests/support/relay.rs`) owns every node's advertised ports and forwards to their bind blocks, with
>     no privilege. Each datagram meets its path's rule: a one-way cut, a loss rate, a hold of `delay ± jitter` (so
>     datagrams reorder) and a duplication rate, every draw from one printed seed (`SLATES_CHAOS_SEED` replays it). A
>     record link's ephemeral source is attributed to its node by the process holding the port (`/proc` on Linux,
>     `netstat` and `ps` on macOS); a datagram no census attributes is dropped and counted, never forwarded, since
>     forwarding it could carry a cut-off node's traffic across.
>   - Nine flows run behind it (`Fleet::start_relayed`), the partitions each against a running process: the nemesis
>     (below) and these eight:
>     - writes streamed while every path holds 20 ms ± 5 ms and loses 1 %, then 5 %, then 1 % with 2 % duplicated, then
>       a takeover over the lossy paths;
>     - an owner cut off both ways, deafened (it speaks and hears nothing) or muted (it hears and nobody hears it), each
>       taken over (`an_owner_partitioned`);
>     - each candidate in turn cut off, deafened or muted for 2 s, with no write refused and no takeover: a partitioned
>       candidate deposes no one, since its view is one voter's and a death needs `f + 1` (A-250)
>       (`candidates_partitioned_in_turn`, the SIGSTOP flow's partition kinds);
>     - one candidate held 200 ms ± 50 ms each way (T-8.3's slow candidate), and no write waits for it: the median write
>       made meanwhile stays under its round trip, since one holder of two makes a write durable at `f = 1`.
>   - Two invariants are judged from outside, in every flow that takes a live volume over (the relayed ones, the
>     SIGSTOP owner and the SIGKILL takeovers: `judge_takeover`, `an_owner_partitioned`). ReadSafety: a latest-state
>     read sent through any node after a write's acknowledgement answers that write or a refusal, never other bytes and
>     never missing; read through every survivor after a takeover, and through a partitioned owner while it runs cut off
>     or the moment its stopped process resumes (its lease lapsed by the clock while it was stopped, before it has heard
>     of its successor). Continuity: the successor's first head is past every position an owner reported durable under
>     an earlier epoch, in the samples or a last look at the owner before its loss, since its log goes on from the head
>     it adopted (`slates_db::live::Shipper::new`).
>   - ReadSafety is judged in the flows that take nothing over too (2026-11-17): the candidates partitioned in turn (all
>     four kinds), the random stalls, the slow candidate and the lossy phases read the stream's newest acknowledged
>     writes through every node mid-fault (halfway through each partition, while the stalls and the slowness last, in
>     each lossy phase) and again once it ends (`judge_reads`). Every read must answer its write or a refusal, through
>     the partitioned node too; the owner must answer every one with its write, since its lease needs one healthy
>     candidate's confirmation of two (§4.8 "Leases and reads"); and at least one read must be judged through every
>     node, the non-vacuity count (a read is judged once it was sent after its write's acknowledgement, which the
>     stream publishes as it goes, `NewestAcknowledged`). Agreement is named for what it is, the models' TotalOrder
>     judged over every copy that answers rather than the committed ones alone.
>   - A seeded nemesis (2026-11-17, `a_seeded_nemesis_of_single_faults_keeps_every_register_invariant`): fourteen
>     single faults drawn from the flow's seed (`SLATES_CHAOS_SEED` replays it), each of seven kinds as likely: every
>     path lossy (one of the lossy profiles), one node slowed 200 ms ± 50 ms, one link severed both ways (a partition
>     that is not transitive: its two ends each still hear the third node), or one node stopped, cut off, deafened or
>     muted. The struck node is the owner as often as either candidate, each fault is held 200 ms to 4 s (a blip under
>     the 900 ms horizon up to past detection and confirmation, so a takeover may finish, or still run, as it ends), and
>     once a run the owner is partitioned until it is taken over. Reads go through every node while each fault lasts,
>     and the fleet must recover whole before the next (members seated, no voter change in flight, neighbourhoods
>     settled, one node shipping, every copy caught up past the owner's durable head), so no cohort loses two members,
>     and the stream, forwarded once another node owns the volume, must make more writes durable meanwhile.
>     It ends with Agreement, NoLoss on the last owner, every copy fenced at its epoch, ReadSafety, Convergence and a
>     write through the last owner, and with Continuity judged from the samples (no head shipped under a fence below
>     what an earlier fence made durable), since its takeovers are unscheduled. Its first runs are the supervisor's.
>   - The client side of StaleNeverCommits in the owner-partition flows is now every write sent to the old owner while
>     it was partitioned refused. Until 2026-11-17 the SIGSTOP flow refused every write sent after the resume instead,
>     but a re-admitted old node forwards a write to the volume's owner (§4.8 "Lookup"), so an acknowledgement through
>     it after the heal can be right; such writes are held to NoLoss on the successor with every other acknowledged one.
>   - The relay's own six tests (in-process sockets, no daemon) pass on macOS (kiln run r265, Adas-MacBook-Pro-2,
>     2026-11-17): forwarding and the answer's way back, a one-way cut, a node muted and deafened, loss, delay and
>     duplication, attribution by process, and the draws. The flows' first runs are the supervisor's (CLAUDE.md §8):
>     `SLATES_TEST_CLI=1 cargo test --release -p slates-cli --test live_chaos -- --test-threads=1` on macOS and Linux.
>   - **First runs (2026-11-18), 11 of 35 flows failed on macOS arm64 (main bfc34cace) and the same on Linux x86_64 and
>     arm64 (69cd38b22).** Linux's census ran there for the first time and attributed every socket but two datagrams.
>     - **Fixed (A-330): the relay never carried the record plane.** The three owner-partition flows failed
>       StaleNeverCommits: their cut-off owners acknowledged 2,086, 3,528 and 2,412 writes after the cut, each durable on
>       a candidate, over record links that went around the relay, since a node announced its record plane at its bound
>       port and formation's redial dialed it. Every relayed flow was vacuous on that plane; each now requires a
>       record-plane datagram per acknowledged write from its relay (`judge_relayed`). Red first:
>       `a_candidate_behind_a_port_mapping_is_redialed_through_it_so_a_cut_there_holds_its_record_plane`
>       (`docs/bugs/2026-11-18-a-redial-went-around-the-port-mapping-the-record-plane-was-announced-at-its-bound-port.md`).
>     - **Fixed (A-334): ReadSafety through a resumed owner.** In the SIGSTOP owner flow the old owner, read the moment it
>       resumed, answered `NotFound` for the successor's acknowledged writes (2.29 s and 3.00 s into the run, 70 to 780
>       ms after their acknowledgements). The flow's new note (`note_missing`) showed why on its first run (Mac Studio,
>       2026-11-18): the old owner had been retired and admitted again under its own id (`fleet_host_epoch` 2), its
>       catalog still held the volume at its epoch-1 shipper, and its lease confirmed again (`lease.wait.parked` 1,
>       `lease.wait.served` 1), so it served its stale copy. A re-admission yielded the host's objects only in its routing
>       table. Now each shard yields its catalogued volumes when its own host's epoch advances (`crate::readmission`): a
>       verb on one is forwarded to the successor, its latest state refused here (`LeaseVerdict::LostToSuccessor`). Red first:
>       `an_owner_admitted_again_forwards_the_volume_its_successor_took_over_and_never_serves_its_own_copy`
>       (`docs/bugs/2026-11-18-an-owner-admitted-again-served-the-copy-its-successor-had-passed.md`). A later takeover
>       naming the host a yielded volume's successor again relinquishes the stale copy and lifts the yield (A-362,

>       yielded volume is refused by its kind on the volume's shard (`remote_attach::lost_attach`; it had attached the

>       **Owed:** releasing a yielded copy's memory (GAP-A9-7).

>       (bounded claims of 12,512 MiB, 782/1024 of it, the flow's own bounded as before): iterations 2, 4 and 5 failed

>       flow's volumes dynamic and the other claims still scaled: 2 of 2 (47 s and 35 s), every probe served 1.92 to
>       9.32 s after its owner's death.
>       **Fixed the same day (A-401): a successor with no room gave up a live volume a survivor held whole.** A candidate
>       now reserves the claim a successor's restore takes as it takes the log's first entry (refused `NoRoom` when it
>       cannot, nothing taken), its copy is charged against that claim, and a successor's restore takes the claim over.
>       Red first, `a_candidates_claim_keeps_the_room_its_successor_makes_the_volume_in`: on main the successor's shard,

>       itself asks every candidate to admit before it records the flag, and refuses `BudgetExceeded` when one cannot
>       (A-401's second part; `a_live_ship_a_candidate_cannot_admit_is_refused_and_ships_once_it_can`). The other 15 flows'
>       single 782 MiB claim (76 % of the runner's 1 GiB shard) is no longer admitted again at a takeover: the successor
>       takes its candidate claim over. The same room is now met at live-ship, typed when it is not (SLATES_DESIGN A-401,
>       "The live chaos flows, in numbers"). The runner's case, six bounded claims on one fleet, is its own flow now:
>       `a_bounded_claim_is_served_by_its_successor_or_refused_before_it_ships` (run request filed 2026-11-18). **Owed:** a
>       candidate that joins the placement later and cannot admit refuses its first entry `NoRoom`, but the configuration
>       may still name it a successor. And the control shard's view of its claims can name one its partition released (a
>       claim admitted for a message the copy then refused is released at the next reconciliation, since only copies
>       holding entries keep theirs), so the copy's next entry is served as claimed with no claim behind it; found
>       reviewing the second part, failing test owed (SLATES_DESIGN A-401, its owed item). `live-ship`'s asks are
>       answered by the partition itself, so they are not misled.

> - **Fixed: a destroy was answered before its tombstone was placed** (record
>   `docs/bugs/2026-11-06-a-destroy-was-answered-before-its-tombstone-was-placed.md`).
>   - With both candidates stopped, a live volume's destroy was answered done; the owner was SIGKILLed, and a survivor
>     listed the volume and served its file again. This is a safety defect.
>   - With a write waiting, the destroy was told `NotFound` by its own teardown, though it happened.
>
>   Every fleet destroy now answers once its tombstone is region-placed (`live_ship::defer_destroy`), and never waits
>   on the live log, so the teardown's `forget` never sees it. Results, live and plain, after the fix: an unheard
>   destroy is never answered done (its client is told the daemon is gone), and a heard one is answered done and stays
>   destroyed across the owner's loss.
> - **Fixed: a write never answered under a partitioned candidate** (record
>   `docs/bugs/2026-11-06-a-call-to-its-own-shard-dropped-its-future-and-a-live-owner-lost-its-sessions.md`).
>   `xshard::task_within` to its own shard dropped its future at the deadline, so a live dispatch on the control shard
>   was dropped mid-exchange. Its borrowed sessions stayed `lent=true` for good (`no_session` 129), and the owner sent to
>   no candidate again. Candidates partitioned in turn (SIGSTOP 2 s each,
>   `candidates_partitioned_in_turn_mid_stream_lose_nothing`) failed 3 of 5 runs before: two writes were never
>   answered, one for over 20 minutes. After the fix, 6 of 7 runs pass and none hangs. Red-checked by
>   `xshard::tests::a_call_to_its_own_shard_runs_its_future_to_the_end_past_the_deadline`.
> - **Open (live-durability): an install never finishes inside the liveness budget, and a dispatch strands its
>   sessions** (record `docs/bugs/2026-11-06-an-install-never-finished-inside-the-liveness-budget.md`).
>   - The size-derived budget is `live_ship::exchange_budget` (`bytes × smoothed RTT / congestion window` plus the
>     liveness budget), on raft-chaos's branch with A-240, where phase one's log fetch uses it. live-durability's
>     lanes take it after A-240 lands. Until then an install over a slow path is cut at the liveness budget, on main
>     and on live-durability's landable branch alike (agreed 2026-11-07).
>   - A candidate left behind the retained tail is sent the whole volume (0.5-1.5 MB) under the 1 s budget an entry
>     gets. In one run 1,391 installs (2.06 GB) went out, both candidates held the owner's head, and no write became
>     durable.
>   - raft-chaos's edits (a size-derived exchange budget, replies folded as they come, a byte-bounded retained tail)
>     are merged into live-durability's dispatch round. It adds one lane per (volume, holder), ships only to candidates
>     holding the catalog, and waits for each exchange's stragglers before a lane ends. A straggler cancelled with its
>     lane had taken its session with it, which is the KIND `wan` stall: both owner sessions `lent=true`, `no_session`
>     24-40 k, runs 42178128960 and 42318867890.
> - **Fixed: an unanswered destroy never settled.** Both candidates stopped, the destroy unanswered (correct), the owner
>   killed. The destroy's records still reach the candidates once they resume, so it takes effect. But the successor,
>   which adopted the tombstone in its takeover and retired it, kept its routing to the volume and answered every verb
>   `Overloaded` for good (`fleet.owner_location.owned_unmaterialized`), while the other survivor answered `NotFound`.
>   That happened in 6 of 6 runs, live and plain, macOS, 2026-11-06. `fleet::retire_shard_tombstones` now forgets the
>   successor's routing at retirement, as a holder does in `tombstone::on_held`. The settled answer for a retired
>   destroyed volume of a departed creator is `OwnerUnreachable`: no member remembers it and its id routes to the gone
>   creator. Nobody lists or serves it. Flow: `a_{live,plain}_volumes_unheard_destroy_then_its_owners_loss`.
> - **Open design item, not built: `NotFound` for a retired destroyed volume of a departed creator.** Today such a
>   volume answers `OwnerUnreachable` (retryable, and true while a takeover could still be pending), because an owner
>   location round never reports an unavailable view as `NotFound` (`owner_location::LocationError`). `NotFound` would
>   be correct once no member can still adopt the id. A node's own view cannot show that: "this node has no unfinished
>   takeover of the creator" is local, and another member may still be mid-adoption of that id, declining for now. So
>   the rule needs the creator's takeover known complete fleet-wide, for example committed in the configuration group,
>   before any member answers `NotFound` for the creator's ids.
> - **Open (live-fixes): the anchored flows fail in fleet membership** on main 76e5b502 with A-228 (macOS, debug, load
>   45-59, 2 runs each).
>   - A candidate's daemon SIGKILLed under its anchor is succeeded in under 1 s but never readmitted within 40 s: the
>     successor holds 3 members with 0 peers probed, while the others hold 2.
>   - A candidate's node replaced by a fresh anchor was promoted to voter after 41 s in one run, and never in the other.
>   These are counted apart from the invariant results.

> - **Fixed (A-240): a live takeover counted members that never held the log** (record
>   `docs/bugs/2026-11-06-a-live-takeover-counted-members-that-never-held-the-log.md`).
>   - Phase one took `f + 1` reports from the current placement. A member placed after the writes (a replacement pod
>     on KIND) stood in for a holder that could not answer, so a stale head could be adopted. KIND runs 42326682216
>     and 42331191530 saw a holder at fence 1 after a takeover at epoch 2. The model broke 10 of 400 seeds.
>   - Each shipper now records its epoch and holders in the volume's catalog and ships only once that catalog is
>     placed at `f + 1`. Phase one counts `f + 1` among those holders alone, and waits typed when too few answer.
>   - The model passes 0 broken of 400 seeds. The process flow is
>     `a_member_that_never_held_the_log_never_stands_in_for_its_holder` (five nodes).
>   - KIND run 42365340676 passed all four profiles end to end with A-240 and the two-step fetch: every write
    acknowledged, every volume taken over whole at epoch 2 (unshaped 2.5 s, wan and wan-loss 16.9 s, ceiling 57.2 s).
  - Process red-check, CI, 13 runs a side: the mutation (counting the current placement) left a holder at fence 1 in 4.
    A-240 left none, and lost no write.
  - **The stack's evidence (CI, 2026-11-07, three-way tree with live-durability's lanes, diag-24).** KIND passed all
    four profiles end to end, every volume taken over whole at epoch 2: unshaped 1,000 writes, p99 1.2 ms, 2.5 s;
    wan 300, p99 423 ms, 17.7 s; wan-loss 300, p99 407 ms, 18.8 s; ceiling 50, p50 1.55 s, 52.6 s. The five-node flow
    passed 7 of 8 with no fence or NoLoss violation, judged on the successor's recorded holders; in its decisive run
    phase one waited 28 times for the stopped holder, then took the volume over whole. The eighth counted
    `fleet.takeover.lost`, and it is explained, no product defect: the flow's expectation was wrong. raft-chaos's diag-28
    run 8 dumped the object's settled cohort [a_old, b, e]: a_old was the replaced member, its RAM gone, and the owner b
    crashed before it had re-shipped and settled onto the new neighbourhood. That is two failures of one cohort at
    f = 1, and §4.8 calls the object lost. raft-chaos's flow now waits for each node's settled generation to equal its
    neighbourhood generation before it crashes the owner. A stall after that wait with no takeover counter moving is
    live-fixes'.
  - **Fixed (2026-11-08): the five-node flow's formation wait demanded a full mesh.** It required every node to have
    probed every other member. §4.8 (amended 2026-10-10) keeps direct contact only with holders and voters, so a
    five-node fleet's two non-voters, which hold nothing for each other, keep no record or probe session once
    formation's first window closes. The flow took them for a stall at 3 of 4 peers probed (diag-live-fixes-30 runs 5
    and 6, diag-raft-chaos-final-39 run 8), with no dial or failure counted, by design.
    - The wait now judges each node's mesh by status's `fleet_peers_in_contact` (above zero) and
      `fleet_peers_unmeshed` (zero), counted over the members held alive (live-fixes, 68fc082f).
    - Two red rounds fixed the rule's two regimes. With the counts over the installed configuration's members, every
      node read both at 0 before the council's first commit, and the wait never ended: diag-raft-chaos-final-41,
      fresh-member 0/8 and kill-at-ack 0/3; diag-raft-chaos-mesh-42 printed (0, 0) with 4 of 4 probed on all five
      nodes.
    - Formation then passed 8 of 8 (diag-raft-chaos-final-43), 11 of 11 (diag-live-fixes-33) and 8 of 8
      (diag-raft-chaos-mesh-48, whose one failure was the register stall above).
  - Fixed (2026-11-07, live-fixes, f2f9477e; the entry "a node back at its anchor with fresh RAM had every pair key
    refused" above): a node replaced at the same machine anchor (same certificate) never answered a live write. Its
    neighbours kept the old node's pair key and refused the new one (`fleet.seal.pair_refused` 789 of 793 served, the
    owner `pair_undelivered` 1,580), so the whole entry never carried their keys (`held_back.keys` 394). Before the
    answering gate such writes were answered and could not be served at a takeover (`takeover_refused.open`). A pair key
    from a successor lineage now retires the old one
    (`docs/bugs/2026-11-07-a-node-back-at-its-anchor-with-fresh-ram-had-every-pair-key-refused.md`): 18 of 18 runs, 15
    of them with a replaced-node owner.
  - **Fixed (2026-11-07): a holder set of 2f+1 under an f-count.** Once the shipper follows the placement, a set can
    have 2f+1 members (the placement moved off the owner: CI diag-20 run 7 recorded e, c, b at f = 1). The shipper
    counted a write durable at f of a set while phase one counts f+1, and 1 + 2 = |H|: the successor counted itself and
    c, and holder b was never fenced. A write is now durable once n − f of a set's n holders hold it, never for n ≤ f
    (live-fixes, 6dd512b4; `a_write_is_durable_only_where_every_takeover_quorum_meets_it`, red on the old count).
  - Open (memory, not safety): a holder a transition dropped keeps its copy, since it is no longer a catalog candidate
    and never sees the record that omits it. A plain release (on that record, or from the owner) can drop the copy of a
    host re-included meanwhile, whose replies the shipper may already count, so it needs a holder-set generation in
    entries and replies (live-fixes; 2ba5572d reverted in eab618f2). Phase one never counts such a copy, and with the
    n − f count no owner commits through it alone.
  - Open: the holder set changing under a live log (joint transition and activation, with live-fixes and raft); a

> 41–45), pushed two increments over four files (accepted 1 and 2; the late overlap refused with `src/one.txt

> written), presented 1 create and 3 replaces (manifest `06ca7f70…`), the human's `slates grant` at the Mac's anchor

> - **The daemon cannot clone an overlay volume.** `admit_clone` gives every clone no host, so `volume clone` of an
>   overlay is refused `ContentUnavailable` (pinned or not; fleet and standalone), though the volume core can.
>   **Fixed 2026-11-18** (g267): a clone of an overlay reads its base through a host of its own that holds every
>   directory of the origin's host under the same handle, each a duplicate descriptor of the very directory the origin
>   reads (`OsHost::try_clone_dirs`), so no outsider's rename or newcomer at a base path can stand in for it; both clone
>   paths take it (the origin's partition, and A-236's alias for a name held on another), and a recovery reopens the
>   clone's base from its record and checks its fingerprints, as it does the origin's. The volume core had a second
>   defect under it: a clone's base plane keyed its root listing by the clone's own root number, while the clone's root
>   directory keeps its origin's, and kept none of the origin's other listings, so a base subdirectory the snapshot
>   already held refused `NotOverlay`; the plane now keys by the snapshot root's number and takes each of the origin's
>   listings with its entries dropped, to be read afresh. Red first:
>   `an_overlays_snapshot_clones_and_each_clone_reads_its_base_across_a_restart` (`crates/server/tests/recovery.rs`)
>   and `a_clones_base_subdirectory_reads_as_the_disk_holds_it` (`crates/vfs/tests/base.rs`); the duplicate's own
>   behaviour by `a_hosts_directories_duplicate_under_the_same_handles_to_the_same_directories`
>   (`crates/base/tests/host.rs`).
> - **No grant can be issued on Linux from the CLI.** The anchor's issuer segment is a descriptor only its children
>   hold (`PRINTS_ISSUER_SURFACE` in `crates/cli/tests/cli.rs`), so a Linux server's landing stops at its
>   presentation. **Closed for the launcher's path (2026-11-18, A-285, fs-server plan step 1):** the launcher (kiln,
>   or this test acting as it) starts the server's anchor with its secret on standard input (A-299) and sets the
>   volume's write policy through `slates-api`; bypass then lands in the one `slates land`, and ask lands once the

>   files) and `an_ask_server_lands_the_client_nodes_merge_once_its_launcher_approves_that_manifest` (the approval

>   container leg of 2026-11-05 stopped at the grant; it now lands. `fs_server.rs`'s `in_a_container` (Linux; gated

>     step is its own kiln command with 1-2 s of dispatch, so on a quiet pair most of a phase is kiln's: g066b and
>     g066c took 47 and 45 s in all. The record sessions' smoothed round trip ran from 17 ms (adacachy at load 34) to
>     724 ms (at load 122.6), with probe timeouts up to 3.3 s.
>   - **One forwarded verb refused `OwnerUnreachable { region: 0 }` (run g066d, about 15:00 UTC, server on adacachy at
>     1750): not reproduced, and the recovery it put in doubt is now a test.** The client's `work` was refused about
>     125 s after the root group formed, after the client's first read of the same green had answered. At the refusal
>     the client node held configuration version 0 with no members while the server held version 1 with both, each node
>     had replaced its record session after a loss 15 (client) and 17 (server) times, and both had a probe session. Its
>     identities phase took 27.7 s (2.8 to 20.6 s in the other runs). It did not recur in the 8 runs after it, 5 of
>     them in the same direction on the same ports, and the run kept no node logs (the program now keeps each node's
>     last 400 lines and its whole status on a failure), so its cause is not known; the refusal itself is the designed
>     one (`verbs::resolve_and_forward` resends to a live owner until the failover SLO, `FAILOVER_SLO_NS`, 10 s, then
>     refuses `OwnerUnreachable`, which a consumer retries). Two causes are ruled out:
>     - Starvation of the server (run g066s2, the same pair and direction): the server node's unit held to a 2% CPU
>       quota (`systemctl --user set-property --runtime UNIT CPUQuota=2%`) for 45 s right after the root group formed
>       and for 30 s while the client made a work; the client held configuration version 1 throughout, every forwarded
>       `work` was answered within 0.5 to 8.6 s, the read after the lift in 0.7 s, and the flow landed exactly the 4
>       merged files.
>     - A link down past the failover delay as the root forms:
>       `a_client_node_cut_off_as_the_root_forms_is_configured_and_forwards_within_its_bound_once_the_link_heals`
>       (`crates/cli/tests/fs_server.rs`) puts every datagram between the two nodes through `live_chaos.rs`'s relay
>       (A-277), cuts it both ways before the server bootstraps the root alone, makes and shares the green while cut,
>       holds the cut 10.9 s (the failover SLO plus a membership horizon) and heals it. The client then held a
>       configuration naming both nodes and answered a forwarded read within a bound derived from its own estimates
>       before the cut (the handshake's initial probe timeout, RFC 9002 §6.2.2; four of the session's probe timeouts;
>       the detector's verdict for the pair, expected arrival plus margin; two coordinator periods; a membership
>       horizon). Forwarded read answered 0.25 to 1.53 s after the heal against bounds of 1.82 to 3.37 s: 13 of 13 on
>       Adas-Mac-Studio (macOS arm64, load 9 to 18) and 18 of 18 on GitHub's ubuntu x86_64 and arm64 runners (diag
>       runs 44342202455, 44342920360 and, merged with main, 44344637800), with 53 to 11,611 datagrams dropped each
>       way at the relay.
>     What remains for g066d is the path itself: the client reached adacachy over the Mac's Wi-Fi. Seen in 2 of those
>     runs and passed to g255 (forward-lane budgets): right after the heal a forward lane's floor read 175 s, past the
>     10 s SLO, from a probe timeout of 24.9 s, about 64 times the session's live one, as if still backed off by the
>     outage (a hypothesis; no log of the backoff count).
>   - Gotcha: a transient unit's service manager substitutes `${NAME}` anywhere in its command (systemd.service(5),
>     "Command lines"; systemd 262), so the first run's `"${f#./}"` reached bash empty and its disk read lost every
>     path while the flow itself passed; the program passes every `$` as `$$`.
> - **Remote attach for writing is done (§4.10; A-222, 2026-11-05).** Another node's `slates attach ID --write`
>   attaches the owner's volume in the record form and `slates write` writes through it
>   (`a_client_node_attaches_a_server_volume_for_writing_and_writes_through_it` in `fs_server.rs`, and the A-222
>   entry above); the two-machine flow still pushes through a green, as an agent's work does. Open, as A-222 records:
>   ownership migration to a writer that stays, and the read-only remote attach of a snapshot.
> - **A self-signed fleet certificate must be a leaf.** OpenSSL's default (`CA:TRUE`) is refused
>   `CaUsedAsEndEntity`; the manifest's documentation does not say so.

> **A green can be shared (fs-server, 2026-11-04).** `share` on a green answered `NotFound`, since it looked the volume up
> by a slot no green has, so only a green's creator could read, work or submit to it: no second consumer, and no user
> of another fleet node. Fixed with its failing test first; record `docs/bugs/2026-11-04-a-green-could-not-be-shared.md`.
> Open, reported there: a green's (and a volume's) name is unique per shard only.

> **Audit of 2dc9f3eb..98000d56 (2026-11-03): defects open, Step 9's evidence holds.** Nine commits made on

> cite was read again: each shows what it is cited for, except one pair of timings A-198 gave the wrong way
> round (corrected there). Zero drives were lost in twenty kills on both Windows architectures, and main CI
> 41565834374 passed 20 of 20 jobs. Open, each owed a failing test first (kiln plan
> 01a1a34bf7e973069e94f773afdea44a, steps 2–8):
> - **vhost-user ring restart (A-169, `663e4df8`): fixed 2026-11-03.** A ring started again after `GET_VRING_BASE`
>   was served from the size, addresses and position it was admitted with. Now a restart resumes only over its

>   never moved, nor one whose stop awaits its chain. Three tests fail on the old seam and pass after; main CI's live
>   QEMU lane passes (41732529738). Owed: an in-place reset, so a rebooted guest keeps its device.

> - **The Windows anchor ended on one malformed or short hold message (A-198): fixed 2026-11-05.** A refusal propagated
>   out of `Supervisor::step` and ended the anchor, whose kill-on-close job then took every held drive. Now it is
>   counted and supervision goes on: 0 anchor exits from 20 bad messages, 20 refusals counted, both holds kept and
>   inherited live, 3 runs each on CI's Windows x86_64 and arm64 (run 41976042550); red on main's sources in run
>   41974533851. The log says each distinct refusal once. A live drive is not sent bad messages, since only the daemon
>   reaches the channel; the live lane passes over the changed drain. Open: the Unix device hold still logs per refusal,
>   and nothing outside the tests reads the refusal count.
>   Record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-03-one-malformed-hold-message-ended-the-windows-anchor.md`.
> - **A refused hold release leaves a held drive (A-198): fixed 2026-11-04 (A-206, run 41978665514; the entry above).** The
>   unmount deleted the file system after the release was refused, so the anchor kept the volume and its drive letter
>   with no daemon serving them (`crates/server/src/winfsp.rs`, `release_hold` and `reap`).
> - **A refused view leaks the held section's handle**: wrong; `view` closed it, and A-205 records the count (see the top of this file).
> - **The receiver's WinFsp guard checks a field WinFsp always zeroes: fixed 2026-11-04 (A-206, runs 41978665514 and
>   41977593496; the entry above).** It read `FileSystem.Version`, not the DLL's version (`FspVersion`). Also, an open whose
>   path was longer than 1024 UTF-16 units was refused, because every open records its kernel name in the held ledger
>   (`crates/bridge-winfsp/src/opens/names.rs`); now slates refuses no path the driver passes.
> - **The receiver that replaced WinFsp's dispatcher: measured, most of its regression fixed, a remainder open (A-212,
>   2026-11-05).** Interleaved on CI's runners against `71cf09ac` (BENCHMARKS, "The WinFsp receiver against the DLL
>   dispatcher", every run), it was worse beyond the spread (arm64 quiet p50: a stat 2.55×, a rename 2.90×, an fsync 1.74×;
>   run 41973314087). Two causes were timed and fixed: a live receive scanned the whole 64 KiB batch tail (26.4 µs on arm64,
>   50.1 µs on x86_64, run 41977769822), and a rename took a shard turn per live open (about 106). After (run 41989009852):
>   arm64 a stat 1.50×, a rename 1.35×, an fsync 1.21×; x86_64 loaded a stat and an open 1.18–1.20×, its quiet runs overlapping. Some loaded tails are far
>   better than the DLL's (x86_64 stat p99 114–133 ms against 0.51–0.60 ms). **Open:** it stays worse beyond the spread at
>   the p50 by about 20 µs a request. The separate response call explains 11–13 µs (winfsp-overlap studies it under A-198's crash
>   rule). **The hops, 2026-11-05:** Open and Release's about 2× was the waiting thread parking; the reply spin cuts arm64 quiet to
>   an fsync 0.88×, a stat 0.89×, a rename 0.90× and x86_64 loaded to 0.77–0.90×, against parking (run 42052991563); its cost is
>   arm64's loaded rename at 1.15×. **Still open:** loaded SetSize's about 4× (the write gap) is a shard preempted just after it
>   answers. Raising shard threads above normal priority removed it (run 42059294312), on arms sharing a machine, so the gain is
>   not yet measured, and it is a whole-daemon change. Also: under two spinners a core on a 4-vCPU x86_64 VM the anchor killed both
>   daemons for a late heartbeat in run 3 of all three jobs that reached it.
> - **The reply spin window can be set by a noisy start (A-212's spin; a measurement defect, 2026-11-06; FIXED
>   2026-11-18, A-560, below).** Each receive worker timed 15 one-way wakes through a bounded channel once as it started
>   and spun for their median before it parked for a reply (`crates/bridge-winfsp/src/reply.rs`, `SAMPLES`). The median was meant to keep
>   one scheduling delay from setting the window, but a start where most samples are delayed sets it too. On CI's arm64
>   runner, quiet, one daemon's two workers measured 143.9 µs and 108.1 µs (diagnostics run 42178889880, run 3), where the
>   other runs' workers measured 4.1–11.5 µs. Such a worker spins up to 144 µs on each slow reply, taking a core from the
>   shards of a 4-vCPU machine. That run's stat p50 (143.0 µs) was no worse than the others' (141.3–151.7 µs), so this is not
>   the receiver's gap against the DLL, but the window has no bound and no check that its samples agree. Owed: a window the
>   measurement cannot set beyond what a wake on the machine costs (a bound derived from the profile's wake, or samples
>   retaken until their spread is within the probe's own precision, as `wake.mean_ns` is), with a test that a delayed start
>   cannot set it. **Fixed by A-560:** the window is learned from the worker's own wakes for its whole life (each reply
>   is stamped at its send, so a reply the worker parked for times its wake), by RFC 6298's estimator (its gains, its
>   seed, and its `S + 4V` band past which a sample is a delay and is folded as the band's edge); it is zero until the
>   wakes agree (the deviation below the RFC's seed, half the wake) and never longer than the step quantum of the shard
>   that started the mount (`crates/bridge-winfsp/src/spin_window.rs`, pure; the start-up probe of 15 is gone). Test:
>   `a_start_of_delayed_wakes_never_spins_past_the_ceiling_and_settles_on_the_wakes` (every host; the old rule's window
>   on its start was 120 µs). **Owed (main's):** the Windows build and the bridge's Windows unit tests
>   (`a_thread_learns_its_window_only_from_the_replies_it_parked_for`), and the WinFsp hops' A/B against A-212's figures.
> - **Two failures recorded open below**: the wake-learning case under load (fixed 2026-11-04, A-199) and the fleet
>   routing Create reply (fixed 2026-11-04 in its fixture; its second, rarer failure fixed 2026-11-05).

> **Empty-wake fixture corrected (2026-11-02, §4.7).** TSan job 125662475876 in main run 41558297045 fails the

> kernel confirmation of a sleeper, using its existing bound; Windows keeps its retained Event. Reply, count and
> deadline assertions are preserved, and the peer is joined on a client error. Native Linux: 100 runs and all nine
> ring cases pass; macOS: nine pass in 0.53 s. The before-fix native 100-run sample passed too; the failing evidence
> is the instrumented CI job. Record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-11-02-an-empty-wake-test-mistook-an-armed-client-for-a-sleeper.md`.

> **Wake-learning failure fixed (2026-11-04, A-199; opened 2026-11-02, A-31).** It was the product, not the fixture's
> one-millisecond delay. A woken client outran its waker, which was preempted between its wake and its
> confirmation. The client's next park cleared the one reply stamp, so the sample was given up, and the late
> confirmation set a bare confirmed bit there that refused the following park's stamp. Logs: in every failing run
> the zero-time out-of-window stamps matched the given-up ones one for one (15 and 15 of 32 at worst). The region
> now holds two stamps, the parks alternate between them, and the parked flag's value names the slot (layout
> version 3). The assertion is unchanged (16 of 32). Interleaved on adacachy, 100 runs each: before 100/100 and
> 89/100 failures on one and two busy CPUs, after 0/100 and 0/100; all nine ring cases on two busy CPUs 95/100
> before, 0/100 after. Record: `docs/bugs/2026-11-04-a-late-wake-confirmation-cost-the-client-two-samples.md`.

> `docs/bugs/2026-11-04-a-survivors-other-shard-never-held-its-live-peer.md`.

> **The wake estimate learns after boot; a long poll is attributed (2026-09-25, A-31).** The boot mean
> was frozen for the process's life although it is ±20–30 % on a VM, and the long-step count read wall
> time, so every preemption of a correct poll counted as the task's bug. Now each shard and each client
> refine an online mean (seeded with the boot mean, weighted over 2^shift wakes from the probe's own
> spread) from the wakes they pay, counting only a sleeper woken: Linux shards confirm by the thread's
> voluntary switches, clients (Linux, macOS) by the daemon's wake finding a sleeper; macOS and Windows
> shards and Windows clients are bounded by the park's announcement, unconfirmed. The quantum, the
> spins, the idle windows and the destroy and archive slices read it live; the client region goes to
> layout version 2. A long poll is the task's (past the quantum on the CPU, or blocked in a call), the
> host's (runnable off the CPU), or unattributed (macOS off the CPU; Windows). Proven by use on both
> hosts (30/30 repeats each); suites green on macOS and Linux; fleet 48/48. Found on the way and owed:
> `ipc_bench`'s parked row times a park-setup race, not a wake (2–18 of 2,000 trips slept); a step costs
> O(ready set), which makes `observe.rs`'s full-arena fill quadratic (95–97 s, before and after); the
> archive walk's unit exceeds the quantum. Record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-09-25-wake-estimate-frozen-at-boot-and-preemptions-counted-as-long-steps.md`.

> **The wake probe measures one event and reports its mean (2026-09-25).** The profile's wake timed
> every park/unpark round trip, mixing an on-CPU handoff (about 0.45 µs) with a real wake (about 10 µs),
> so runs split between the two (median 416 ns or 10,041 ns on the same container cores), and it
> converged the median while consumers read a p99 that was often the maximum of 64 samples. Now: the
> waiter confirmed asleep, the pair placed as production is, the mean converged (the spin-then-park
> threshold is the expected cost of parking; a spinning waiter never saw the tail, a parked one did),
> five rounds compared by their medians. Quiet-host containers: median 8.9–10.8 µs over ten runs, mean
> 15.1–17.6 µs on four CPUs; macOS mean 2.03–3.27 µs over nine. Spin window, step quantum and timer
> tick read the mean; the inbound ring the p99 at its overflow target. The boot mean being quick on a VM
> and the long-step count reading wall time were closed by A-31 (the entry above).
> Record: `docs/bugs/2026-09-22-wake-probe-mixes-two-events-and-reports-an-unconverged-tail.md`.

> **Client ring sized by Little's law (2026-09-22).** A daemon's client seats followed one boot
> measurement of the wake tail: `slots_per_ring` was `wake.p99 / syscall.median`, and the bulk area
> scales with it, so pods of one image seated 1 to 1285 clients. A one-seat KIND pod refused the lane's
> `bootstrap` while its readiness probe held the seat; CI's macOS runner seated two and refused the
> restart test's third. The ring is now §4.7's Little's law, `requests_in_flight_per_shard` rounded to
> a power of two; the regression fails before with CI's exact message and passes after; workspace,
> server, fleet (48/48) and CLI-flow suites pass; every pod of a two-CPU fresh-cluster KIND run seats
> 330. Owed: the wake probe's mixed events and unconverged p99 still feed the step budget, the spin
> window and the runtime's inbound ring; the pressure hold follows host-wide memory.
> Record: `docs/bugs/2026-09-22-client-ring-sized-by-the-wake-tail-not-littles-law.md`.

> **KIND takeover: council seats (2026-09-22).** CI run 35615113353's KIND lane retired the killed
> owner but never took its volume over. The council's voters were the lowest member ids up to
> `2f + 1`: the owner's replacement, admitted beside its unretired predecessor, took the live
> leader's seat while the dead predecessor kept its own, and the replacement, which cannot observe
> its own predecessor's death, then led a council that never retired it. A sitting voter now keeps
> its seat while it is a member, and a freed seat goes only to a member the leader holds alive; the
> id is only the tiebreak. Reproduced one failure in eight on a CPU-pinned local cluster; the fixed
> image passed 6 of 6; two deterministic council regressions; 152 cluster unit tests and the fleet
> suite pass. Owed: the replacement's blind spot after two overlapping faults, and root-group
> representatives chosen by id order. KIND initial formation (run 35615970514) stays open and was
> not reproduced (14 local formations, each within 0.3 s).

> counters and checks the replacement bytes. Records: the 2026-09-20 differential-oracle,
> host-digest-test and pjdfstest-device-fixture bug documents.

> **Real landing gate (2026-09-20).** The Linux crash/resume run exposed the exchange's
> own ctime update being mistaken for an outsider edit. The engine now verifies the actual
> displaced name and hashes its witnessed content when ctime changed. The simulator models
> that update; 18 landing oracle tests and all five real Linux landing tests pass (0.06 s
> for the latter). Symlinks reported as ENOTDIR now receive the intended EscapesTarget
> refusal. The next CLI gate exposed a BSD-only mktemp template; its repair is in validation.

> **OCI source integration (2026-09-20).** The macOS CLI gate reaches a real capability
> mount but the OCI verifier still expected the former bare source. Its matcher now checks
> the exact volume and capability syntax, removing the bearer suffix from evidence and
> refusals. Eight pure checks pass; the real container workload is being rerun. Record:
> `docs/bugs/2026-09-20-oci-verifier-rejects-capability-mounts.md`.

> **Attachment lifecycle repair (2026-09-20).** OCI bindings now borrow their checked
> source mount, survive the issuing CLI and daemon restart, and end on explicit detach or
> parent unmount. The strict crash/rights lifecycle passes in 7.90 s; the current real Docker
> and CLI suite passes all 10 cases in 28.85 s, retaining exact detach assertions.
> The two-owner SIGKILL regression passes in 3.81 s after moving SDK retirement across all
> owner shards. Fresh client identities are now reserved durably before handoff: the crash
> probe exposed a new `Status` receiving an old `Created` completion. Linux workspace:
> 1,554 passed, zero failed, 14 ignored; macOS: 1,546 passed, zero failed, 14 ignored.
> The later last-id restart history passes on both hosts. Queued-forward
> and publication-refusal proofs remain owed. The corrected snapshot comparison passes;
> nine other macOS performance ceilings remain red, and the intermittent destroy failure
> remains open. Commands, scope and logs are recorded in TBD_FIXES.

> **CI coverage correction (2026-09-20).** The Linux CLI step now supplies `/dev/shm`
> for the portable operator-key recovery test. It previously returned without executing;
> with RAM supplied its unchanged real CLI history passes in 0.42 s. The native macOS
> SDK packaging commands pass with Ada's requested Python 3.14.3 (five Python, five direct
> Node and three packaged Node tests, no skips). Linux loom and shuttle pass too. Miri's
> Linux x86-64 interpretation passes 82 cases with 11 existing exclusions; memory and
> wire leak checks stay enabled. These results do not close instruction-count, KIND,
> Windows or performance obligations.

> **Shard-count correction (2026-09-20).** Choose an explicit shard count before deriving
> capacities. The old override left a one-shard SDK daemon with a three-shard memory split
> and allowed a six-shard daemon's content/metadata backing alone to exceed its 4 GiB bound.
> Two live-daemon regressions fail before the fix and pass after it (1.42 s, macOS).
> The unchanged Linux SDK packaging suite now passes all 13 cases with zero skips. The
> Linux workspace passes 1,557 cases, including all 49 fleet histories; strict Clippy,
> xtask, non-root FUSE and the real CLI step pass too. macOS passes 1,548 workspace cases,
> all 48 fleet histories, the real CLI lifecycle and 13 installed SDK cases; see
> [the diagnosis](../bugs/2026-09-20-explicit-shards-keep-the-automatic-memory-split.md).
